12870.label: Job 1:1
12870.text: There was a man in the land of Uz whose name was Job. He was an upright man of integrity; he feared God and shunned what was bad.

12871.label: Job 1:2
12871.text: Seven sons and three daughters were born to him.

12872.label: Job 1:3
12872.text: His livestock amounted to 7,000 sheep, 3,000 camels, 1,000 cattle, and 500 donkeys, along with a very large number of servants, so that he became the greatest of all the people of the East.

12873.label: Job 1:4
12873.text: Each of his sons would hold a banquet at his house on his own set day. They would invite their three sisters to eat and drink with them.

12874.label: Job 1:5
12874.text: After a series of banquet days was complete, Job would send for them in order to sanctify them. Then he would get up early in the morning and offer up burnt sacrifices for each of them. For Job said: “Maybe my sons have sinned and have cursed God in their heart.” That is what Job would always do.

12875.label: Job 1:6
12875.text: Now the day came when the sons of the true God entered to take their station before Jehovah, and Satan also entered among them.

12876.label: Job 1:7
12876.text: Then Jehovah said to Satan: “Where have you come from?” Satan answered Jehovah: “From roving about on the earth and from walking about in it.”

12877.label: Job 1:8
12877.text: And Jehovah said to Satan: “Have you taken note of my servant Job? There is no one like him on the earth. He is an upright man of integrity, fearing God and shunning what is bad.”

12878.label: Job 1:9
12878.text: At that Satan answered Jehovah: “Is it for nothing that Job has feared God?

12879.label: Job 1:10
12879.text: Have you not put up a protective hedge around him and his house and everything he has? You have blessed the work of his hands, and his livestock has spread out in the land.

12880.label: Job 1:11
12880.text: But, for a change, stretch out your hand and strike everything he has, and he will surely curse you to your very face.”

12881.label: Job 1:12
12881.text: Then Jehovah said to Satan: “Look! Everything that he has is in your hand. Only do not lay your hand on the man himself!” So Satan went out from the presence of Jehovah.

12882.label: Job 1:13
12882.text: Now on the day when his sons and daughters were eating and drinking wine in their oldest brother’s house,

12883.label: Job 1:14
12883.text: a messenger came to Job and said: “The cattle were plowing and the donkeys were grazing beside them

12884.label: Job 1:15
12884.text: when the Sa·beʹans attacked and took them, and they killed the servants with the sword. I am the only one who escaped to tell you.”

12885.label: Job 1:16
12885.text: While he was still speaking, another one came and said: “Fire from God fell from the heavens and blazed among the sheep and the servants and consumed them! I am the only one who escaped to tell you.”

12886.label: Job 1:17
12886.text: While he was still speaking, another one came and said: “The Chal·deʹans formed three bands and made a raid on the camels and took them, and they killed the servants with the sword. I am the only one who escaped to tell you.”

12887.label: Job 1:18
12887.text: While he was still speaking, yet another one came and said: “Your sons and your daughters were eating and drinking wine in their oldest brother’s house.

12888.label: Job 1:19
12888.text: Suddenly a great wind came from the wilderness, and it struck the four corners of the house, so that it fell on the young people and they were killed. I am the only one who escaped to tell you.”

12889.label: Job 1:20
12889.text: At that Job got up and ripped apart his garment and cut the hair off his head; then he fell to the ground and bowed down

12890.label: Job 1:21
12890.text: and said: “Naked I came out of my mother’s womb,And naked I will return. Jehovah has given, and Jehovah has taken away. Let the name of Jehovah continue to be praised.”

12891.label: Job 1:22
12891.text: In all of this, Job did not sin or accuse God of doing anything wrong.

12892.label: Job 2:1
12892.text: Afterward the day came when the sons of the true God entered to take their station before Jehovah, and Satan also entered among them to take his station before Jehovah.

12893.label: Job 2:2
12893.text: Then Jehovah said to Satan: “Where have you come from?” Satan answered Jehovah: “From roving about on the earth and from walking about in it.”

12894.label: Job 2:3
12894.text: And Jehovah said to Satan: “Have you taken note of my servant Job? There is no one like him on the earth. He is an upright man of integrity, fearing God and shunning what is bad. He is still holding firmly to his integrity, even though you try to incite me against him to destroy him for no reason.”

12895.label: Job 2:4
12895.text: But Satan answered Jehovah: “Skin for skin. A man will give everything that he has for his life.

12896.label: Job 2:5
12896.text: But, for a change, stretch out your hand and strike his bone and flesh, and he will surely curse you to your very face.”

12897.label: Job 2:6
12897.text: Then Jehovah said to Satan: “Look! He is in your hand! Only do not take his life!”

12898.label: Job 2:7
12898.text: So Satan went out from the presence of Jehovah and struck Job with painful boils from the sole of his foot to the crown of his head.

12899.label: Job 2:8
12899.text: And Job took a piece of broken pottery to scrape himself, and he was sitting among the ashes.

12900.label: Job 2:9
12900.text: Finally his wife said to him: “Are you still holding firmly to your integrity? Curse God and die!”

12901.label: Job 2:10
12901.text: But he said to her: “You are talking like one of the senseless women. Should we accept only what is good from the true God and not accept also what is bad?” In all of this, Job did not sin with his lips.

12902.label: Job 2:11
12902.text: Three companions of Job heard about all the calamities that had come upon him, and each came from his own place—Elʹi·phaz the Teʹman·ite, Bilʹdad the Shuʹhite, and Zoʹphar the Naʹa·ma·thite. So they agreed to meet together to go and sympathize with Job and comfort him.

12903.label: Job 2:12
12903.text: When they saw him from a distance, they did not recognize him. They began to weep loudly and to rip their garments apart, and they threw dust into the air and onto their heads.

12904.label: Job 2:13
12904.text: Then they sat on the ground with him for seven days and seven nights. No one said a word to him, for they saw that his pain was very great.

12905.label: Job 3:1
12905.text: It was after this that Job began to speak and to curse the day of his birth.

12907.label: Job 3:3
12907.text: “Let the day perish on which I was born, Also the night when someone said: ‘A man has been conceived!’

12908.label: Job 3:4
12908.text: Let that day be darkness. Let God above show no concern for it;Let no light shine upon it.

12909.label: Job 3:5
12909.text: Let the deepest darkness reclaim it. Let a rain cloud settle over it. Let whatever darkens the day terrify it.

12910.label: Job 3:6
12910.text: That night—let the gloom seize it; Let it not rejoice among the days of a year,And let it not enter among the number of the months.

12911.label: Job 3:7
12911.text: Indeed! Let that night become barren;Let no joyful cry be heard in it.

12912.label: Job 3:8
12912.text: Let those who curse the day put a curse on it,Those who are able to awaken Le·viʹa·than.

12913.label: Job 3:9
12913.text: Let the stars of its twilight grow dark;Let it wait in vain for daylight,And let it not see the rays of dawn.

12914.label: Job 3:10
12914.text: For it did not close the doors of my mother’s womb; Nor did it hide trouble from my eyes.

12915.label: Job 3:11
12915.text: Why did I not die at birth? Why did I not perish when I came from the womb?

12916.label: Job 3:12
12916.text: Why were there knees to receive meAnd breasts to nurse me?

12917.label: Job 3:13
12917.text: For now I would be lying down undisturbed; I would be sleeping and at rest

12918.label: Job 3:14
12918.text: With kings of the earth and their advisers,Who built for themselves places that are now in ruins,

12919.label: Job 3:15
12919.text: Or with princes who possessed gold,Whose houses were filled with silver.

12920.label: Job 3:16
12920.text: Or why was I not like a hidden miscarriage,Like children who have never seen the light?

12921.label: Job 3:17
12921.text: There even the wicked have ceased from agitation;There the weary are at rest.

12922.label: Job 3:18
12922.text: There the prisoners are at ease together;They do not hear the voice of the one forcing them to work.

12923.label: Job 3:19
12923.text: Small and great are the same there, And the slave is set free from his master.

12924.label: Job 3:20
12924.text: Why does he give light to one who is sufferingAnd life to those in bitter distress?

12925.label: Job 3:21
12925.text: Why do they long for death, but it does not come? They dig for it more than for hidden treasures,

12926.label: Job 3:22
12926.text: Those who are rejoicing greatly,Who are happy when they find the grave.

12927.label: Job 3:23
12927.text: Why does he give light to a man who has lost his way,Whom God has hedged in?

12928.label: Job 3:24
12928.text: For in place of my food comes my sighing, And my groaning pours out like water.

12929.label: Job 3:25
12929.text: For what I have dreaded has come upon me,And what I have feared has befallen me.

12930.label: Job 3:26
12930.text: I have had no peace, no quiet, no rest,But trouble keeps coming.”

12931.label: Job 4:1
12931.text: Elʹi·phaz the Teʹman·ite then said in reply:

12932.label: Job 4:2
12932.text: “If someone tries to speak to you, will you become impatient? For who can hold back from speaking?

12933.label: Job 4:3
12933.text: True, you have corrected many,And you used to strengthen the weak hands.

12934.label: Job 4:4
12934.text: Your words would raise up anyone stumbling,And you would strengthen those whose knees were buckling.

12935.label: Job 4:5
12935.text: But now it has happened to you, and you are overwhelmed; It touches you, and you are dismayed.

12936.label: Job 4:6
12936.text: Does your reverence for God not give you confidence? Does your way of integrity not give you hope?

12937.label: Job 4:7
12937.text: Remember, please: What innocent person has ever perished? When have the upright ever been destroyed?

12938.label: Job 4:8
12938.text: What I have seen is that those who plow what is harmfulAnd those who sow trouble will reap the same.

12939.label: Job 4:9
12939.text: By the breath of God they perish,And through a blast of his anger they come to an end.

12940.label: Job 4:10
12940.text: The lion roars, and a young lion growls,But even the teeth of strong lions are broken.

12941.label: Job 4:11
12941.text: A lion perishes for lack of prey,And the cubs of a lion are scattered.

12942.label: Job 4:12
12942.text: Now a word was brought to me in secret,And a whisper of it reached my ear.

12943.label: Job 4:13
12943.text: In troubling thoughts during visions of the night,When deep sleep falls upon men,

12944.label: Job 4:14
12944.text: A terrible trembling came upon me,Filling all my bones with dread.

12945.label: Job 4:15
12945.text: A spirit passed over my face;The hair of my flesh bristled.

12946.label: Job 4:16
12946.text: It then stood still,But I did not recognize its appearance. A form was in front of my eyes;There was a calm, and then I heard a voice:

12947.label: Job 4:17
12947.text: ‘Can a mortal man be more righteous than God? Can a man be cleaner than his own Maker?’

12948.label: Job 4:18
12948.text: Look! He has no faith in his servants,And he finds fault with his angels.

12949.label: Job 4:19
12949.text: How much more so with those dwelling in houses of clay,Whose foundation is in the dust, Who are crushed as easily as a moth!

12950.label: Job 4:20
12950.text: They are completely crushed from morning to evening;They perish forever, and no one takes notice.

12951.label: Job 4:21
12951.text: Are they not like a tent whose cord is pulled out? They die without wisdom.

12952.label: Job 5:1
12952.text: “Call, please! Is there anyone answering you? To which of the holy ones will you turn?

12953.label: Job 5:2
12953.text: For resentment will kill the foolish one,And envy will put the simpleminded to death.

12954.label: Job 5:3
12954.text: I have seen the foolish one taking root,But suddenly his dwelling place is cursed.

12955.label: Job 5:4
12955.text: His sons are far from safety,And they are crushed at the city gate, with no one to save them.

12956.label: Job 5:5
12956.text: The hungry one eats what he harvests,Taking it even from among the thorns,And their possessions are ensnared.

12957.label: Job 5:6
12957.text: For harmful things do not sprout from the dust,And trouble does not spring from the ground.

12958.label: Job 5:7
12958.text: For man is born for trouble,As surely as sparks fly upward.

12959.label: Job 5:8
12959.text: But I would appeal to God,And to God I would submit my case,

12960.label: Job 5:9
12960.text: To the One doing great and unsearchable things,Wonderful things without number.

12961.label: Job 5:10
12961.text: He gives rain to the earthAnd sends waters upon the fields.

12962.label: Job 5:11
12962.text: He raises the lowly up high,And he raises up the dejected one to salvation.

12963.label: Job 5:12
12963.text: He frustrates the schemes of the crafty,So that the work of their hands does not succeed.

12964.label: Job 5:13
12964.text: He catches the wise in their own cunning, So that the plans of the shrewd are thwarted.

12965.label: Job 5:14
12965.text: They meet with darkness during the day,And they grope about at midday as if it were night.

12966.label: Job 5:15
12966.text: He saves from the sword of their mouth,Saving the poor from the hand of the strong,

12967.label: Job 5:16
12967.text: So that there is hope for the lowly,But the mouth of unrighteousness is shut.

12968.label: Job 5:17
12968.text: Look! Happy is the man whom God reproves;So do not reject the discipline of the Almighty!

12969.label: Job 5:18
12969.text: For he causes pain, but binds up the wound;He breaks apart, but heals with his own hands.

12970.label: Job 5:19
12970.text: He will save you from six calamities,Even the seventh will not harm you.

12971.label: Job 5:20
12971.text: During famine he will redeem you from death,And from the power of a sword during war.

12972.label: Job 5:21
12972.text: You will be protected from the lash of the tongue, And you will not fear devastation when it comes.

12973.label: Job 5:22
12973.text: You will laugh at destruction and hunger,And you will not fear the wild beasts of the earth.

12974.label: Job 5:23
12974.text: For the stones of the field will not harm you, And the wild beasts of the field will be at peace with you.

12975.label: Job 5:24
12975.text: You will know that your tent is secure, And nothing will be missing when you inspect your pasture.

12976.label: Job 5:25
12976.text: You will enjoy many children,And your descendants will be as plentiful as the vegetation of the earth.

12977.label: Job 5:26
12977.text: You will still be strong when you go to the grave,Like sheaves of grain gathered in their season.

12978.label: Job 5:27
12978.text: Look! We have investigated this, and it is so. Listen and accept it.”

12980.label: Job 6:2
12980.text: “If only my anguish could be fully weighedAnd put on scales together with my calamity!

12981.label: Job 6:3
12981.text: For now it is heavier than the sands of the seas. That is why my words have been wild talk.

12982.label: Job 6:4
12982.text: For the arrows of the Almighty have pierced me,And my spirit is drinking their venom; The terrors from God are lined up against me.

12983.label: Job 6:5
12983.text: Will a wild donkey cry out when it has grass,Or will a bull bellow when it has fodder?

12984.label: Job 6:6
12984.text: Is tasteless food eaten without salt,Or is there flavor in the juice of a mallow?

12985.label: Job 6:7
12985.text: I have refused to touch such things. They are like contamination in my food.

12986.label: Job 6:8
12986.text: O that my request would be realizedAnd that God would grant my desire!

12987.label: Job 6:9
12987.text: That God would be willing to crush me,And that he would reach out his hand and do away with me!

12988.label: Job 6:10
12988.text: For even that would bring me comfort;I would leap for joy despite the unrelenting pain,For I have not denied the sayings of the Holy One.

12989.label: Job 6:11
12989.text: Do I have the strength to keep waiting? And what end awaits me, that I should continue to live?

12990.label: Job 6:12
12990.text: Is my strength like that of rock? Or is my flesh made of copper?

12991.label: Job 6:13
12991.text: Is there any way that I can help myselfWhen all my means of support has been driven from me?

12992.label: Job 6:14
12992.text: Anyone who withholds loyal love from his fellow man Will forsake the fear of the Almighty.

12993.label: Job 6:15
12993.text: My own brothers have been as treacherous as a winter stream,Like the water of winter streams that dry up.

12994.label: Job 6:16
12994.text: They are darkened by ice,And in them the melting snow is hidden.

12995.label: Job 6:17
12995.text: But in due season they become waterless and come to an end;When it becomes hot, they dry up.

12996.label: Job 6:18
12996.text: Their course is diverted;They flow into the desert and vanish.

12997.label: Job 6:19
12997.text: The caravans of Teʹma look for them;The travelers from Sheʹba wait for them.

12998.label: Job 6:20
12998.text: They are ashamed because of their misplaced trust;They come there only to be disappointed.

12999.label: Job 6:21
12999.text: For this is how you have become to me; You have seen the terror of my calamity, and you are afraid.

13000.label: Job 6:22
13000.text: Have I said, ‘Give me something,’ Or requested that you make a gift for me from your wealth?

13001.label: Job 6:23
13001.text: Have I asked to be rescued from the hand of an enemyOr to be saved from oppressors?

13002.label: Job 6:24
13002.text: Instruct me, and I will be silent; Help me to understand my mistake.

13003.label: Job 6:25
13003.text: Honest words are not painful! But what benefit can be found in your reproof?

13004.label: Job 6:26
13004.text: Are you scheming to reprove my words,A desperate man’s sayings, which the wind blows away?

13005.label: Job 6:27
13005.text: You would also cast lots over an orphan And sell your own friend!

13006.label: Job 6:28
13006.text: So now turn and look at me,For I would not lie to your very faces.

13007.label: Job 6:29
13007.text: Reconsider, please—do not misjudge me—Yes, reconsider, for my righteousness is yet intact.

13008.label: Job 6:30
13008.text: Is my tongue speaking unjustly? Does my palate not discern that something is wrong?

13009.label: Job 7:1
13009.text: “Is not the life of mortal man on earth like compulsory labor,And are not his days like those of a hired worker?

13010.label: Job 7:2
13010.text: Like a slave, he longs for the shadow,And like a hired worker, he waits for his wages.

13011.label: Job 7:3
13011.text: Thus I have been assigned months of futilityAnd nights of misery have been counted out for me.

13012.label: Job 7:4
13012.text: When I lie down I ask, ‘When will I get up?’ But as the night drags on, I toss restlessly until the dawning of the day.

13013.label: Job 7:5
13013.text: My flesh is covered with maggots and clods of dirt; My skin is full of scabs and pus.

13014.label: Job 7:6
13014.text: My days go by more quickly than a weaver’s shuttle, And they come to an end without hope.

13015.label: Job 7:7
13015.text: Remember that my life is wind, That my eye will never again see happiness.

13016.label: Job 7:8
13016.text: The eye that sees me now will see me no more;Your eyes will look for me, but I will be gone.

13017.label: Job 7:9
13017.text: Like a cloud that fades and vanishes,The one who goes down to the Grave does not come back up.

13018.label: Job 7:10
13018.text: He will not return again to his house,And his place will acknowledge him no more.

13019.label: Job 7:11
13019.text: Therefore, I will not restrain my mouth. I will speak in the anguish of my spirit;I will complain in my bitter distress!

13020.label: Job 7:12
13020.text: Am I the sea or a sea monster,That you should set a guard over me?

13021.label: Job 7:13
13021.text: When I say, ‘My couch will comfort me;My bed will help ease my misery,’

13022.label: Job 7:14
13022.text: Then you terrify me with dreamsAnd frighten me with visions,

13023.label: Job 7:15
13023.text: So that I would choose suffocation,Yes, death rather than this body of mine.

13024.label: Job 7:16
13024.text: I loathe my life; I do not want to go on living. Leave me alone, for my days are like a breath.

13025.label: Job 7:17
13025.text: What is mortal man that you should concern yourself with himAnd fix your attention on him?

13026.label: Job 7:18
13026.text: Why do you inspect him every morningAnd test him every moment?

13027.label: Job 7:19
13027.text: Will you not look away from meAnd leave me alone long enough to swallow my saliva?

13028.label: Job 7:20
13028.text: If I have sinned, how could I harm you, the Observer of mankind? Why have you made me your target? Have I become a burden to you?

13029.label: Job 7:21
13029.text: Why do you not pardon my transgressionAnd excuse my error? For soon I will lie down in the dust, And you will look for me, but I will be gone.”

13030.label: Job 8:1
13030.text: Bilʹdad the Shuʹhite then said in reply:

13031.label: Job 8:2
13031.text: “How long will you keep speaking like this? The words of your mouth are but a mighty wind!

13032.label: Job 8:3
13032.text: Will God pervert justice,Or will the Almighty pervert righteousness?

13033.label: Job 8:4
13033.text: If your sons sinned against him,He let them be punished for their revolt;

13034.label: Job 8:5
13034.text: But if you would just look to God And plead with the Almighty for favor,

13035.label: Job 8:6
13035.text: And if you were truly pure and upright, He would pay attention to you And restore you to your rightful place.

13036.label: Job 8:7
13036.text: And though your beginning was small,Your future would be great.

13037.label: Job 8:8
13037.text: Ask, please, the former generation,And pay attention to the things their fathers found out.

13038.label: Job 8:9
13038.text: For we were born only yesterday, and we know nothing,Because our days on earth are a shadow.

13039.label: Job 8:10
13039.text: Will they not instruct youAnd tell you what they know?

13040.label: Job 8:11
13040.text: Will a papyrus plant grow tall where there is no marsh? Will a reed grow tall without water?

13041.label: Job 8:12
13041.text: While it is still in the bud, not yet plucked off,It will dry up before any other plant.

13042.label: Job 8:13
13042.text: This is the outcome of all who forget God,For the hope of the godless will perish,

13043.label: Job 8:14
13043.text: Whose confidence is in vainAnd whose trust is as fragile as a spider’s web.

13044.label: Job 8:15
13044.text: He will lean against his house, but it will not keep standing;He will try to hold on to it, but it will not last.

13045.label: Job 8:16
13045.text: He is a moist plant in the sunlight,And his shoots spread out in the garden.

13046.label: Job 8:17
13046.text: In a heap of stones, his roots become entwined;He looks for a house among the stones.

13047.label: Job 8:18
13047.text: But when he is uprooted from his place,That place will deny him and say, ‘I have never seen you.’

13048.label: Job 8:19
13048.text: Yes, that is how he will disappear; Then others will spring up from the dust.

13049.label: Job 8:20
13049.text: Surely God will not reject those who keep integrity; Nor will he support evil men,

13050.label: Job 8:21
13050.text: For he will yet fill your mouth with laughterAnd your lips with shouts of joy.

13051.label: Job 8:22
13051.text: Those hating you will be clothed with shame,And the tent of wicked ones will be no more.”

13053.label: Job 9:2
13053.text: “For a fact I know that this is so. But how can mortal man be in the right in a case with God?

13054.label: Job 9:3
13054.text: If someone wishes to argue with Him, That one could not answer one of His questions in a thousand.

13055.label: Job 9:4
13055.text: He is wise in heart and mighty in power. Who can resist him and come off uninjured?

13056.label: Job 9:5
13056.text: He moves mountains without anyone knowing it;He overturns them in his anger.

13057.label: Job 9:6
13057.text: He shakes the earth out of its place,So that its pillars tremble.

13058.label: Job 9:7
13058.text: He commands the sun not to shineAnd seals off the light of the stars;

13059.label: Job 9:8
13059.text: He spreads out the heavens by himself, And he treads upon the high waves of the sea.

13060.label: Job 9:9
13060.text: He made the Ash, the Keʹsil, and the Kiʹmah constellations, And the constellations of the southern sky;

13061.label: Job 9:10
13061.text: He does great and unsearchable things, Wonderful things that cannot be counted.

13062.label: Job 9:11
13062.text: He passes by me, and I cannot see him;He moves past me, but I do not discern him.

13063.label: Job 9:12
13063.text: When he snatches something, who can resist him? Who can say to him, ‘What are you doing?’

13064.label: Job 9:13
13064.text: God will not restrain his anger; Even the helpers of Raʹhab will bow down to him.

13065.label: Job 9:14
13065.text: How much more when I answer himMust I choose my words carefully to argue with him!

13066.label: Job 9:15
13066.text: Even if I were in the right, I would not answer him. I could only plead for mercy from my judge.

13067.label: Job 9:16
13067.text: If I call out to him, will he answer me? I do not believe that he will listen to my voice,

13068.label: Job 9:17
13068.text: For he crushes me with a stormAnd multiplies my wounds for no reason.

13069.label: Job 9:18
13069.text: He does not let me catch my breath;He keeps filling me with bitter things.

13070.label: Job 9:19
13070.text: If it is a matter of power, he is the strong one. If it is a matter of justice, he says: ‘Who can call me to account?’

13071.label: Job 9:20
13071.text: If I were in the right, my own mouth would condemn me;Even if I keep my integrity, he will declare me guilty.

13072.label: Job 9:21
13072.text: Even if I keep my integrity, I am not confident about myself; I reject this life of mine.

13073.label: Job 9:22
13073.text: It is all the same. That is why I say,‘He destroys the innocent and the wicked alike.’

13074.label: Job 9:23
13074.text: If a flash flood should cause sudden death,He would mock at the despair of the innocent.

13075.label: Job 9:24
13075.text: The earth has been handed over to the wicked; He covers the eyes of its judges. If it is not he, then, who is it?

13076.label: Job 9:25
13076.text: Now my days are swifter than a runner; They run away without seeing good.

13077.label: Job 9:26
13077.text: They glide by like reed boats,Like eagles that swoop down on their prey.

13078.label: Job 9:27
13078.text: If I say, ‘I will forget my complaint,I will change my expression and be cheerful,’

13079.label: Job 9:28
13079.text: I would still be afraid because of all my pains, And I know you would not find me innocent.

13080.label: Job 9:29
13080.text: I would be found guilty. So why should I struggle in vain?

13081.label: Job 9:30
13081.text: If I wash myself in water from melting snow,And I cleanse my hands in lye,

13082.label: Job 9:31
13082.text: Then you would dip me in a pit,So that even my own garments would detest me.

13083.label: Job 9:32
13083.text: For he is not a man like me that I may answer him,That we should go to court together.

13084.label: Job 9:33
13084.text: There is no person to decide between us,Who could serve as our judge.

13085.label: Job 9:34
13085.text: If he would stop beating me And not let his terror frighten me,

13086.label: Job 9:35
13086.text: Then I would speak to him unafraid,For it is not in me to speak out of fear.

13087.label: Job 10:1
13087.text: “I loathe my life. I will give vent to my complaints. I will speak out in my bitter distress!

13088.label: Job 10:2
13088.text: I will say to God: ‘Do not pronounce me guilty. Tell me why you are contending with me.

13089.label: Job 10:3
13089.text: Does it benefit you to oppress,To despise the work of your hands While you favor the advice of the wicked?

13090.label: Job 10:4
13090.text: Do you have eyes of flesh,Or do you see as mortal man does?

13091.label: Job 10:5
13091.text: Are your days like the days of mortals,Or are your years like those of a man,

13092.label: Job 10:6
13092.text: That you should search out my errorAnd keep looking for my sin?

13093.label: Job 10:7
13093.text: You know that I am not guilty; And no one can save me from your hand.

13094.label: Job 10:8
13094.text: Your own hands have shaped me and made me, But now you would completely destroy me.

13095.label: Job 10:9
13095.text: Remember, please, that you made me out of clay, But now you make me return to dust.

13096.label: Job 10:10
13096.text: Did you not pour me out like milkAnd curdle me like cheese?

13097.label: Job 10:11
13097.text: With skin and flesh you clothed me,And with bones and sinews you wove me together.

13098.label: Job 10:12
13098.text: You have given me life and loyal love;You have guarded my spirit with your care.

13099.label: Job 10:13
13099.text: But you secretly intended to do these things. I know that these things are from you.

13100.label: Job 10:14
13100.text: If I sinned, you would watch me, And you would not acquit me of my error.

13101.label: Job 10:15
13101.text: If I am guilty, too bad for me! And even if I am innocent, I cannot raise my head, For I am filled with dishonor and affliction.

13102.label: Job 10:16
13102.text: If I raise my head up, you hunt for me like a lion And again show your power against me.

13103.label: Job 10:17
13103.text: You bring new witnesses against meAnd increase your anger against me,As hardship after hardship comes upon me.

13104.label: Job 10:18
13104.text: So why did you bring me out from the womb? I should have died before any eye could see me.

13105.label: Job 10:19
13105.text: It would have been as though I never existed;I would have been taken straight from the womb to the grave.’

13106.label: Job 10:20
13106.text: Are not my days few? Let him leave me alone;Let him turn his eyes away from me, so that I may find some relief

13107.label: Job 10:21
13107.text: Before I go away—and I will not return —To the land of deepest darkness,

13108.label: Job 10:22
13108.text: To the land of utter gloom,A land of deep shadow and disorder,Where even the light is like the gloom.”

13109.label: Job 11:1
13109.text: Zoʹphar the Naʹa·ma·thite said in reply:

13110.label: Job 11:2
13110.text: “Will all these words go unanswered,Or will a lot of talking make someone right?

13111.label: Job 11:3
13111.text: Will your empty talk silence people? Will no one rebuke you for your mocking words?

13112.label: Job 11:4
13112.text: For you say, ‘My teaching is pure, And I am clean in your eyes.’

13113.label: Job 11:5
13113.text: But if only God would speakAnd open his lips to you!

13114.label: Job 11:6
13114.text: Then he would reveal to you the secrets of wisdom,For practical wisdom has many sides. Then you would realize that God allows some of your error to be forgotten.

13115.label: Job 11:7
13115.text: Can you discover the deep things of GodOr discover everything about the Almighty?

13116.label: Job 11:8
13116.text: It is higher than heaven. What can you accomplish? It is deeper than the Grave. What can you know?

13117.label: Job 11:9
13117.text: It is longer than the earthAnd broader than the sea.

13118.label: Job 11:10
13118.text: If he passes by and detains someone and convenes a court,Who can resist him?

13119.label: Job 11:11
13119.text: For he knows when men are deceitful. When he sees what is evil, will he not take notice?

13120.label: Job 11:12
13120.text: But an empty-headed man will understandOnly when a wild donkey can give birth to a man.

13121.label: Job 11:13
13121.text: If only you would prepare your heartAnd stretch out your hands to him.

13122.label: Job 11:14
13122.text: If your hand is doing wrong, put it far away,And let no unrighteousness dwell in your tents.

13123.label: Job 11:15
13123.text: For then you could lift up your face with no defect;You could stand firm, free of fear.

13124.label: Job 11:16
13124.text: For then you will forget your trouble;You will remember it as waters that have flowed past you.

13125.label: Job 11:17
13125.text: Your life will become brighter than midday;Even its darkness will be like the morning.

13126.label: Job 11:18
13126.text: You will be confident because there is hope,And you will look around and lie down in security.

13127.label: Job 11:19
13127.text: You will lie down, with no one to make you afraid,And many people will seek your favor.

13128.label: Job 11:20
13128.text: But the eyes of the wicked will fail;And they will find no place to escape,And their only hope will be death.”

13130.label: Job 12:2
13130.text: “Surely you are the people who know, And wisdom will die out with you!

13131.label: Job 12:3
13131.text: But I too have understanding. I am not inferior to you. Who does not know these things?

13132.label: Job 12:4
13132.text: I have become a laughingstock to my companions, One calling to God for an answer. A righteous and blameless man is a laughingstock.

13133.label: Job 12:5
13133.text: The carefree person has contempt for calamity,Thinking it is only for those whose feet are unsteady.

13134.label: Job 12:6
13134.text: The tents of robbers are at peace, And those who provoke God are secure, Those who have their god in their hands.

13135.label: Job 12:7
13135.text: However, ask, please, the animals, and they will instruct you;Also the birds of the heavens, and they will tell you.

13136.label: Job 12:8
13136.text: Or give consideration to the earth, and it will instruct you;And the fish of the sea will declare it to you.

13137.label: Job 12:9
13137.text: Who among all these does not knowThat the hand of Jehovah has done this?

13138.label: Job 12:10
13138.text: In his hand is the life of every living thing And the spirit of every human.

13139.label: Job 12:11
13139.text: Does not the ear test out wordsAs the tongue tastes food?

13140.label: Job 12:12
13140.text: Is not wisdom found among the aged, And does not understanding come with a long life?

13141.label: Job 12:13
13141.text: With him there are wisdom and mightiness; He has counsel and understanding.

13142.label: Job 12:14
13142.text: When he tears something down, it cannot be rebuilt; What he has shut, no man can open.

13143.label: Job 12:15
13143.text: When he withholds the waters, everything dries up; When he sends them out, they overwhelm the earth.

13144.label: Job 12:16
13144.text: With him there are strength and practical wisdom; To him belong the one going astray and the one leading astray;

13145.label: Job 12:17
13145.text: He makes counselors go barefoot, And he makes fools of judges.

13146.label: Job 12:18
13146.text: He loosens the bonds imposed by kings, And he binds a belt around their waist.

13147.label: Job 12:19
13147.text: He makes priests walk barefoot, And he overthrows those who are firmly established in power;

13148.label: Job 12:20
13148.text: He deprives trusted advisers of speechAnd takes away the sensibleness of old men;

13149.label: Job 12:21
13149.text: He pours out contempt upon nobles, And he makes powerful ones weak;

13150.label: Job 12:22
13150.text: He reveals deep things from the darkness, And he brings deep darkness into the light;

13151.label: Job 12:23
13151.text: He makes nations grow great in order to destroy them;He enlarges nations, that he may lead them into exile.

13152.label: Job 12:24
13152.text: He takes away the understanding of the leaders of the peopleAnd makes them wander in trackless wastelands.

13153.label: Job 12:25
13153.text: They grope in darkness, where there is no light;He makes them wander about like drunken men.

13154.label: Job 13:1
13154.text: “Yes, my eye has seen all of this,My ear has heard and understood it.

13155.label: Job 13:2
13155.text: What you know, I also know;I am not inferior to you.

13156.label: Job 13:3
13156.text: For my part, I would rather speak to the Almighty himself;I desire to argue my case with God.

13157.label: Job 13:4
13157.text: But you are smearing me with lies;All of you are useless physicians.

13158.label: Job 13:5
13158.text: If only you would keep absolutely silent,That would show wisdom on your part.

13159.label: Job 13:6
13159.text: Listen, please, to my arguments,And pay attention to the pleadings of my lips.

13160.label: Job 13:7
13160.text: Will you speak unjustly on God’s behalf,And will you speak deceitfully for him?

13161.label: Job 13:8
13161.text: Will you take his side, Will you try to plead the case of the true God?

13162.label: Job 13:9
13162.text: Would it turn out well if he examined you? Will you fool him as you would a mortal man?

13163.label: Job 13:10
13163.text: He will surely rebuke youIf you secretly try to show favoritism.

13164.label: Job 13:11
13164.text: Will not his very dignity terrify youAnd the dread of him fall upon you?

13165.label: Job 13:12
13165.text: Your wise sayings are proverbs of ashes;Your defenses are as fragile as defenses of clay.

13166.label: Job 13:13
13166.text: Keep silent before me, so that I may speak. Then let whatever may come upon me come!

13167.label: Job 13:14
13167.text: Why do I put myself in danger And take my life in my hands?

13168.label: Job 13:15
13168.text: Though he may slay me, I would still wait; I would argue my case before his face.

13169.label: Job 13:16
13169.text: He would then become my salvation, For no godless person may come in before him.

13170.label: Job 13:17
13170.text: Listen closely to my word;Pay attention to my declaration.

13171.label: Job 13:18
13171.text: See, now, I have prepared my legal case;I know I am in the right.

13172.label: Job 13:19
13172.text: Who will contend with me? I would die if I were to stay silent!

13173.label: Job 13:20
13173.text: Only grant two things to me, O God, So that I will not conceal myself from before you:

13174.label: Job 13:21
13174.text: Remove your heavy hand far away from me,And do not let the fear of you terrify me.

13175.label: Job 13:22
13175.text: Either call and I will answer,Or let me speak, and you answer me.

13176.label: Job 13:23
13176.text: What are my errors and sins? Reveal to me my transgression and my sin.

13177.label: Job 13:24
13177.text: Why do you hide your face And consider me your enemy?

13178.label: Job 13:25
13178.text: Will you try to frighten a windblown leafOr chase after dry stubble?

13179.label: Job 13:26
13179.text: For you keep recording bitter accusations against me,And you make me answer for the sins of my youth.

13180.label: Job 13:27
13180.text: You have put my feet in stocks,You scrutinize all my paths,And you trace out each of my footprints.

13181.label: Job 13:28
13181.text: So man decays like something rotten,Like a garment eaten by moths.

13182.label: Job 14:1
13182.text: “Man, born of woman,Is short-lived and filled with trouble.

13183.label: Job 14:2
13183.text: He comes up like a blossom and then withers away; He flees like a shadow and disappears.

13184.label: Job 14:3
13184.text: Yes, you have fixed your eye upon him,And you bring him into judgment with yourself.

13185.label: Job 14:4
13185.text: Who can produce someone clean from someone unclean? No one can!

13186.label: Job 14:5
13186.text: If his days are decided,The number of his months is with you;You have set a limit for him that he may not go beyond.

13187.label: Job 14:6
13187.text: Turn your gaze away from him so that he may rest,Until, like a hired worker, he finishes out his day.

13188.label: Job 14:7
13188.text: For there is hope even for a tree. If it is cut down, it will sprout again,And its twigs will continue to grow.

13189.label: Job 14:8
13189.text: If its root grows old in the groundAnd its stump dies in the soil,

13190.label: Job 14:9
13190.text: At the scent of water it will sprout;And it will produce branches like a new plant.

13191.label: Job 14:10
13191.text: But a man dies and lies powerless;When a human expires, where is he?

13192.label: Job 14:11
13192.text: Waters disappear from the sea,And a river drains away and dries up.

13193.label: Job 14:12
13193.text: Man also lies down and does not get up. Until heaven is no more, they will not wake up,Nor will they be aroused from their sleep.

13194.label: Job 14:13
13194.text: O that in the Grave you would conceal me, That you would hide me until your anger passes by,That you would set a time limit for me and remember me!

13195.label: Job 14:14
13195.text: If a man dies, can he live again? I will wait all the days of my compulsory serviceUntil my relief comes.

13196.label: Job 14:15
13196.text: You will call, and I will answer you. You will long for the work of your hands.

13197.label: Job 14:16
13197.text: But for now, you keep counting my every step;You watch only for my sin.

13198.label: Job 14:17
13198.text: My transgression is sealed up in a bag,And you seal up my error with glue.

13199.label: Job 14:18
13199.text: As a mountain falls and crumbles awayAnd a rock is dislodged from its place,

13200.label: Job 14:19
13200.text: As water wears away stonesAnd its torrents wash away earth’s soil,So you have destroyed the hope of mortal man.

13201.label: Job 14:20
13201.text: You keep overpowering him until he perishes; You change his appearance, and you send him away.

13202.label: Job 14:21
13202.text: His sons are honored, but he does not know it;They become insignificant, but he does not realize it.

13203.label: Job 14:22
13203.text: He feels pain only while he is still in his flesh;He mourns only while he is still alive.”

13204.label: Job 15:1
13204.text: Elʹi·phaz the Teʹman·ite said in reply:

13205.label: Job 15:2
13205.text: “Will a wise person answer with empty arguments, Or will he fill his belly with the east wind?

13206.label: Job 15:3
13206.text: Reproving with mere words is useless,And talk alone is of no benefit.

13207.label: Job 15:4
13207.text: For you undermine the fear of God,And you diminish any concern for God.

13208.label: Job 15:5
13208.text: For your error dictates what you say, And you choose crafty speech.

13209.label: Job 15:6
13209.text: Your own mouth condemns you, and not I;Your own lips testify against you.

13210.label: Job 15:7
13210.text: Were you the first man ever born,Or was your birth before that of the hills?

13211.label: Job 15:8
13211.text: Do you listen to the confidential talk of God,Or do you limit wisdom to yourself?

13212.label: Job 15:9
13212.text: What do you know that we do not know? What do you understand that we do not?

13213.label: Job 15:10
13213.text: Both the gray-haired and the aged are among us, Men much older than your father.

13214.label: Job 15:11
13214.text: Are God’s consolations not enough for you,Or words spoken gently to you?

13215.label: Job 15:12
13215.text: Why does your heart carry you away,And why do your eyes flash with anger?

13216.label: Job 15:13
13216.text: For you turn your spirit against God himself,And you allow such words to go out of your own mouth.

13217.label: Job 15:14
13217.text: What is mortal man that he should be pure,Or anyone born of a woman that he should be righteous?

13218.label: Job 15:15
13218.text: Look! He has no faith in his holy ones,And even the heavens are not pure in his eyes.

13219.label: Job 15:16
13219.text: How much less so when a person is detestable and corrupt, A man who drinks in unrighteousness just like water!

13220.label: Job 15:17
13220.text: I will inform you; listen to me! I will relate what I have seen,

13221.label: Job 15:18
13221.text: What wise men have related from their fathers, Things they have not hidden.

13222.label: Job 15:19
13222.text: To them alone the land was given,And no stranger passed among them.

13223.label: Job 15:20
13223.text: A wicked person suffers torment all his days,Throughout all the years reserved for the tyrant.

13224.label: Job 15:21
13224.text: Terrifying sounds are in his ears; In a time of peace, marauders attack him.

13225.label: Job 15:22
13225.text: He does not believe that he will escape from darkness; He is reserved for a sword.

13226.label: Job 15:23
13226.text: He wanders about in search of food —where is it? He well knows that the day of darkness is at hand.

13227.label: Job 15:24
13227.text: Distress and anguish keep terrifying him;They overpower him like a king ready to launch an attack.

13228.label: Job 15:25
13228.text: For he raises his hand against God himselfAnd tries to defy the Almighty;

13229.label: Job 15:26
13229.text: He stubbornly rushes against Him,With his thick, strong shield;

13230.label: Job 15:27
13230.text: His face is covered with fat,And his hips bulge with fat;

13231.label: Job 15:28
13231.text: He resides in cities that will be brought to ruin,In houses where no one will dwell,Which will become heaps of stones.

13232.label: Job 15:29
13232.text: He will not grow rich, and his wealth will not accumulate,Nor will his possessions spread over the land.

13233.label: Job 15:30
13233.text: He will not escape from darkness;A flame will dry up his twig, And he will pass away by a blast of God’s mouth.

13234.label: Job 15:31
13234.text: He should not go astray and trust in what is worthless,For what he gets in exchange will be worthless;

13235.label: Job 15:32
13235.text: It will happen before his day,And his branches will never flourish.

13236.label: Job 15:33
13236.text: He will be like a vine that shakes off its unripe grapes,And like an olive tree that casts off its blossoms.

13237.label: Job 15:34
13237.text: For the assembly of godless ones is sterile, And fire will consume the tents of bribery.

13238.label: Job 15:35
13238.text: They conceive trouble and give birth to what is wicked,And their womb produces deceit.”

13240.label: Job 16:2
13240.text: “I have heard many things like these before. All of you are troublesome comforters!

13241.label: Job 16:3
13241.text: Is there an end to empty words? What provokes you to answer this way?

13242.label: Job 16:4
13242.text: I could also speak as you do. If you were in my place, I could make persuasive speeches against youAnd shake my head at you.

13243.label: Job 16:5
13243.text: Instead, though, I would strengthen you with the words of my mouth,And the consolation of my lips would bring relief.

13244.label: Job 16:6
13244.text: If I speak, my own pain is not relieved, And if I stop speaking, how much is my pain reduced?

13245.label: Job 16:7
13245.text: But now he has made me weary; He has devastated my whole household.

13246.label: Job 16:8
13246.text: You also seize me, and it has become a witness,So that my own skinniness rises up and testifies to my face.

13247.label: Job 16:9
13247.text: His anger has torn me to pieces, and he harbors animosity against me. He grinds his teeth against me. My adversary pierces me with his eyes.

13248.label: Job 16:10
13248.text: They have opened their mouth wide against me, And they have scornfully struck my cheeks;In large numbers they gather against me.

13249.label: Job 16:11
13249.text: God hands me over to young boys,And he thrusts me into the hands of the wicked.

13250.label: Job 16:12
13250.text: I was untroubled, but he shattered me; He grabbed me by the back of the neck and crushed me;Then he set me up as his target.

13251.label: Job 16:13
13251.text: His archers surround me; He pierces my kidneys and feels no compassion;He pours out my gall on the earth.

13252.label: Job 16:14
13252.text: He breaks through against me with breach after breach;He rushes at me like a warrior.

13253.label: Job 16:15
13253.text: I have sewn sackcloth together to cover my skin, And I have buried my dignity in the dust.

13254.label: Job 16:16
13254.text: My face is red from weeping, And on my eyelids is deep shadow,

13255.label: Job 16:17
13255.text: Although my hands have done no violenceAnd my prayer is pure.

13256.label: Job 16:18
13256.text: O earth, do not cover my blood! And let there be no resting-place for my outcry!

13257.label: Job 16:19
13257.text: Even now, my witness is in the heavens;The one who can testify for me is in the heights.

13258.label: Job 16:20
13258.text: My companions ridicule me As my eye sheds tears to God.

13259.label: Job 16:21
13259.text: Let someone arbitrate between a man and God,As one would between a man and his fellow.

13260.label: Job 16:22
13260.text: For the years to come are few,And I will go away on the path of no return.

13261.label: Job 17:1
13261.text: “My spirit has been broken, my days have been extinguished;The graveyard awaits me.

13262.label: Job 17:2
13262.text: Mockers surround me, And my eye must gaze at their rebellious behavior.

13263.label: Job 17:3
13263.text: Please accept my security, and keep it with you. Who else will shake hands with me and pledge in my behalf?

13264.label: Job 17:4
13264.text: For you have concealed discernment from their heart; That is why you do not exalt them.

13265.label: Job 17:5
13265.text: He may offer to share with his friends,While the eyes of his children fail.

13266.label: Job 17:6
13266.text: He has made me an object of scorn among the peoples, So that I became one in whose face they spit.

13267.label: Job 17:7
13267.text: From anguish my eyes grow dim, And all my limbs are but a shadow.

13268.label: Job 17:8
13268.text: Upright people stare in amazement at this,And the innocent one is disturbed over the godless.

13269.label: Job 17:9
13269.text: The righteous one keeps holding fast to his way, And the one with clean hands grows stronger.

13270.label: Job 17:10
13270.text: However, you may all come and resume your arguing,For I have not found anyone wise among you.

13271.label: Job 17:11
13271.text: My days are finished; My plans, the desires of my heart, have been shattered.

13272.label: Job 17:12
13272.text: They keep turning night into day,Saying, ‘Light must be near because it is dark.’

13273.label: Job 17:13
13273.text: If I wait, the Grave will become my home; I will spread out my bed in darkness.

13274.label: Job 17:14
13274.text: I will call out to the pit, ‘You are my father!’ To the maggot, ‘My mother and my sister!’

13275.label: Job 17:15
13275.text: Where, then, is my hope? Who can see hope for me?

13276.label: Job 17:16
13276.text: It will go down to the barred gates of the Grave When we all descend together into the dust.”

13277.label: Job 18:1
13277.text: Bilʹdad the Shuʹhite said in reply:

13278.label: Job 18:2
13278.text: “How long before you stop making such speeches? Show some understanding so that we may then speak.

13279.label: Job 18:3
13279.text: Why should we be viewed as animals And be considered stupid in your eyes?

13280.label: Job 18:4
13280.text: Even if you tear yourself to pieces in your anger,Will the earth be abandoned for your sake,Or will the rock move away from its place?

13281.label: Job 18:5
13281.text: Yes, the light of the wicked will be extinguished,And the flame of his fire will not shine.

13282.label: Job 18:6
13282.text: The light in his tent will certainly grow dark,And the lamp over him will be extinguished.

13283.label: Job 18:7
13283.text: His vigorous stride is shortened,And his own counsel will make him fall.

13284.label: Job 18:8
13284.text: For his feet will lead him into a net,And he will wander onto its mesh.

13285.label: Job 18:9
13285.text: A trap will seize him by the heel;A snare will catch him.

13286.label: Job 18:10
13286.text: A rope is hidden for him on the ground,And a trap lies in his path.

13287.label: Job 18:11
13287.text: Terrors frighten him on all sides And chase him at his feet.

13288.label: Job 18:12
13288.text: His strength fails him,And disaster will make him stagger.

13289.label: Job 18:13
13289.text: His skin is eaten away;The most deadly disease consumes his limbs.

13290.label: Job 18:14
13290.text: He is torn away from the security of his tent And marched to the king of terrors.

13291.label: Job 18:15
13291.text: Strangers will live in his tent;Sulfur will be scattered on his home.

13292.label: Job 18:16
13292.text: His roots will dry up beneath him,And his branches will wither above him.

13293.label: Job 18:17
13293.text: The memory of him will fade from the earth,And in the street his name will be unknown.

13294.label: Job 18:18
13294.text: He will be driven from the light into the darknessAnd chased away from the productive land.

13295.label: Job 18:19
13295.text: He will have no offspring and no descendants among his people,And he will be without a survivor in the place where he lives.

13296.label: Job 18:20
13296.text: When his day comes, the people in the West will be appalledAnd the people in the East will be seized with horror.

13297.label: Job 18:21
13297.text: This is what happens to the tents of a wrongdoerAnd to the place of the one who has not known God.”

13299.label: Job 19:2
13299.text: “How long will you keep irritating my soul, Crushing me with words?

13300.label: Job 19:3
13300.text: These ten times you have rebuked me;You are not ashamed to deal harshly with me.

13301.label: Job 19:4
13301.text: And if indeed I made a mistake,My error remains with me.

13302.label: Job 19:5
13302.text: If you insist on exalting yourselves over me,Claiming that the reproach against me is justified,

13303.label: Job 19:6
13303.text: Know, then, that it is God who has misled me,And he has caught me in his hunting net.

13304.label: Job 19:7
13304.text: Look! I keep crying out, ‘Violence!’ but I get no answer; I keep crying for help, but there is no justice.

13305.label: Job 19:8
13305.text: My path he has blocked with a stone wall, and I cannot pass by;He has covered my roadways with darkness.

13306.label: Job 19:9
13306.text: He has stripped me of my gloryAnd removed the crown from my head.

13307.label: Job 19:10
13307.text: He breaks me down on all sides until I perish;My hope he uproots like a tree.

13308.label: Job 19:11
13308.text: His anger burns against me,And he views me as his enemy.

13309.label: Job 19:12
13309.text: His troops come together and besiege me,And they camp around my tent.

13310.label: Job 19:13
13310.text: My own brothers he has driven far away from me,And those who know me have turned away from me.

13311.label: Job 19:14
13311.text: My close companions are gone,And those whom I knew well have forgotten me.

13312.label: Job 19:15
13312.text: Guests in my house and my slave girls consider me a stranger;I am a foreigner in their eyes.

13313.label: Job 19:16
13313.text: I call for my servant, but he does not respond;With my mouth I beg him for compassion.

13314.label: Job 19:17
13314.text: My very breath has become loathsome to my wife, And I am a stench to my own brothers.

13315.label: Job 19:18
13315.text: Even young children despise me;When I rise up, they begin jeering at me.

13316.label: Job 19:19
13316.text: All my close friends detest me, And those whom I loved have turned against me.

13317.label: Job 19:20
13317.text: My bones stick to my skin and my flesh, And I escape with the skin of my teeth.

13318.label: Job 19:21
13318.text: Show me mercy, my companions, show me mercy,For God’s own hand has touched me.

13319.label: Job 19:22
13319.text: Why do you keep persecuting me as God does, Attacking me without letup?

13320.label: Job 19:23
13320.text: If only my words were written down,If only they could be inscribed in a book!

13321.label: Job 19:24
13321.text: O that they were carved forever in the rock,With an iron stylus and lead!

13322.label: Job 19:25
13322.text: For I well know that my redeemer is alive;He will come later and rise up over the earth.

13323.label: Job 19:26
13323.text: After my skin has thus been destroyed,While yet in my flesh, I will see God,

13324.label: Job 19:27
13324.text: Whom I will see for myself,Whom my own eyes will see, not someone else’s. But deep inside I feel overwhelmed!

13325.label: Job 19:28
13325.text: For you say, ‘In what way are we persecuting him?’ Since the root of the problem is with me.

13326.label: Job 19:29
13326.text: Be in fear of the sword yourselves, For the sword brings punishment against errors;You should know that there is a judge.”

13327.label: Job 20:1
13327.text: Zoʹphar the Naʹa·ma·thite said in reply:

13328.label: Job 20:2
13328.text: “This is why my own troubling thoughts urge me to answerBecause of the agitation I feel.

13329.label: Job 20:3
13329.text: I have heard a reproof that insults me;And my understanding impels me to reply.

13330.label: Job 20:4
13330.text: Surely you must have always known this,For it has been so since man was put on the earth,

13331.label: Job 20:5
13331.text: That the joyful cry of the wicked is briefAnd the rejoicing of the godless one is for a moment.

13332.label: Job 20:6
13332.text: Although his greatness ascends to heavenAnd his head reaches to the clouds,

13333.label: Job 20:7
13333.text: He will perish forever like his own dung;Those who used to see him will say, ‘Where is he?’

13334.label: Job 20:8
13334.text: He will fly off like a dream, and they will not find him;He will be chased away like a vision of the night.

13335.label: Job 20:9
13335.text: The eye that once saw him will not do so again,And his place will behold him no more.

13336.label: Job 20:10
13336.text: His own children will seek the favor of the poor,And his own hands will give back his wealth.

13337.label: Job 20:11
13337.text: His bones were full of youthful vigor,But it will lie down with him in mere dust.

13338.label: Job 20:12
13338.text: If what is bad tastes sweet in his mouth,If he hides it under his tongue,

13339.label: Job 20:13
13339.text: If he savors it and does not let it goBut keeps holding it in his mouth,

13340.label: Job 20:14
13340.text: His food will turn sour inside him;It will become like the poison of cobras within him.

13341.label: Job 20:15
13341.text: He has swallowed down wealth, but he will vomit it up;God will empty it out of his belly.

13342.label: Job 20:16
13342.text: The venom of cobras he will suck;The fangs of a viper will kill him.

13343.label: Job 20:17
13343.text: He will never see the streams of water,The torrents of honey and butter.

13344.label: Job 20:18
13344.text: He will give back his goods without consuming them; He will not enjoy the wealth from his trade.

13345.label: Job 20:19
13345.text: For he has crushed and abandoned the poor;He has seized a house that he did not build.

13346.label: Job 20:20
13346.text: But he will feel no peace within himself;His wealth will not help him escape.

13347.label: Job 20:21
13347.text: There is nothing left for him to devour;That is why his prosperity will not last.

13348.label: Job 20:22
13348.text: When his wealth reaches its peak, anxiety will overtake him;The full force of misfortune will come against him.

13349.label: Job 20:23
13349.text: As he fills his belly,God will send his burning anger upon him,Raining it down upon him into his bowels.

13350.label: Job 20:24
13350.text: When he flees from weapons of iron,Arrows from a copper bow will pierce him.

13351.label: Job 20:25
13351.text: He pulls an arrow from his back,A glittering weapon from his gall,And terror seizes him.

13352.label: Job 20:26
13352.text: Total darkness awaits his treasures;A fire that no one fanned will consume him;Calamity awaits any survivors in his tent.

13353.label: Job 20:27
13353.text: Heaven will uncover his error;The earth will rise up against him.

13354.label: Job 20:28
13354.text: A flood will sweep his house away;It will be a heavy torrent on the day of God’s anger.

13355.label: Job 20:29
13355.text: This is the wicked man’s share from God,The inheritance that God has decreed for him.”

13357.label: Job 21:2
13357.text: “Listen carefully to what I say;Let this be the consolation you give me.

13358.label: Job 21:3
13358.text: Bear with me while I speak;After I speak, you may then mock me.

13359.label: Job 21:4
13359.text: Is my complaint directed toward a man? If it were, would I not lose patience?

13360.label: Job 21:5
13360.text: Look at me and stare in amazement;Put your hand over your mouth.

13361.label: Job 21:6
13361.text: When I think about it, I am disturbed,And my whole body shudders.

13362.label: Job 21:7
13362.text: Why do the wicked live on, Grow old, and become wealthy?

13363.label: Job 21:8
13363.text: Their children are always in their presence,And they get to see their descendants.

13364.label: Job 21:9
13364.text: Their houses are secure, they are free from fear, And God does not punish them with his rod.

13365.label: Job 21:10
13365.text: Their bulls breed without failure;Their cows give birth and do not miscarry.

13366.label: Job 21:11
13366.text: Their boys run outside just like a flock,And their children skip about.

13367.label: Job 21:12
13367.text: They sing accompanied by tambourine and harpAnd rejoice at the sound of the flute.

13368.label: Job 21:13
13368.text: They spend their days in contentmentAnd go down peacefully to the Grave.

13369.label: Job 21:14
13369.text: But they say to the true God, ‘Leave us alone! We have no desire to know your ways.

13370.label: Job 21:15
13370.text: Who is the Almighty, that we should serve him? What would we gain by being acquainted with him?’

13371.label: Job 21:16
13371.text: But I know that they do not control their own prosperity. The thinking of the wicked is far from me.

13372.label: Job 21:17
13372.text: How often is the lamp of the wicked extinguished? How often does disaster come upon them? How often does God deal out destruction to them in his anger?

13373.label: Job 21:18
13373.text: Do they ever become like straw before the windAnd like chaff that a storm wind carries away?

13374.label: Job 21:19
13374.text: God will store up a man’s punishment for his own sons. But may God repay him so that he will know it.

13375.label: Job 21:20
13375.text: May his own eyes see his ruin,And may he be the one to drink from the rage of the Almighty.

13376.label: Job 21:21
13376.text: For what does he care about what happens to his house after himIf the number of his months is cut short?

13377.label: Job 21:22
13377.text: Can anyone teach knowledge to God, When He is the one who judges even the highest ones?

13378.label: Job 21:23
13378.text: One man dies in his full vigor When he is completely carefree and at ease,

13379.label: Job 21:24
13379.text: When his thighs are padded with fatAnd his bones are strong.

13380.label: Job 21:25
13380.text: But another man dies deeply distressed, Never having tasted good things.

13381.label: Job 21:26
13381.text: Together they will lie down in the dust, And maggots will cover both of them.

13382.label: Job 21:27
13382.text: Look! I know exactly what you are thinkingAnd the schemes you devise to wrong me.

13383.label: Job 21:28
13383.text: For you say, ‘Where is the house of the prominent man,And where is the tent in which the wicked one lived?’

13384.label: Job 21:29
13384.text: Have you not questioned travelers? Do you not carefully study their observations,

13385.label: Job 21:30
13385.text: That an evil person is spared on the day of disasterAnd rescued on the day of fury?

13386.label: Job 21:31
13386.text: Who will confront him about his way,And who will repay him for what he has done?

13387.label: Job 21:32
13387.text: When he is carried to the graveyard,A vigil will be kept over his tomb.

13388.label: Job 21:33
13388.text: The clods of earth of the valley will be sweet to him, And all mankind follows after him Like the countless number before him.

13389.label: Job 21:34
13389.text: So why offer me meaningless comfort? There is nothing but deceit in your answers!”

13390.label: Job 22:1
13390.text: Elʹi·phaz the Teʹman·ite said in reply:

13391.label: Job 22:2
13391.text: “Can a man be of use to God? Can anyone with insight be of benefit to him?

13392.label: Job 22:3
13392.text: Does the Almighty care that you are righteous,Or does he gain anything because you follow the course of integrity?

13393.label: Job 22:4
13393.text: Will he punish youAnd enter into judgment with you for your reverence?

13394.label: Job 22:5
13394.text: Is it not because your own wickedness is so greatAnd there is no end to your errors?

13395.label: Job 22:6
13395.text: For you seize a pledge from your brothers for no reason,And you strip people of their garments, leaving them naked.

13396.label: Job 22:7
13396.text: You do not give the tired one a drink of water,And you hold back food from the hungry.

13397.label: Job 22:8
13397.text: The land belongs to the powerful man, And the favored one dwells in it.

13398.label: Job 22:9
13398.text: But you sent away widows empty-handed,And you crushed the arms of fatherless children.

13399.label: Job 22:10
13399.text: That is why you are surrounded by traps, And sudden terrors frighten you;

13400.label: Job 22:11
13400.text: That is why it is so dark that you cannot see,And a flood of water covers you.

13401.label: Job 22:12
13401.text: Is not God in the heights of heaven? And see how high all the stars are.

13402.label: Job 22:13
13402.text: But you have said: ‘What does God really know? Can he judge through thick gloom?

13403.label: Job 22:14
13403.text: Clouds screen him off so that he does not seeAs he walks about on the vault of heaven.’

13404.label: Job 22:15
13404.text: Will you follow the ancient pathThat wicked men have walked,

13405.label: Job 22:16
13405.text: Men who have been snatched away before their time,Whose foundation was washed away by a flood?

13406.label: Job 22:17
13406.text: They were saying to the true God: ‘Leave us alone!’ And ‘What can the Almighty do to us?’

13407.label: Job 22:18
13407.text: Yet, he is the One who filled their houses with good things. (Such wicked thinking is far from my own.)

13408.label: Job 22:19
13408.text: The righteous will see this and rejoice,And the innocent will mock them and say:

13409.label: Job 22:20
13409.text: ‘Our opponents have been destroyed,And a fire will consume what is left of them.’

13410.label: Job 22:21
13410.text: Get to know Him, and you will be at peace;Then good things will come your way.

13411.label: Job 22:22
13411.text: Accept the law from his mouth,And keep his sayings in your heart.

13412.label: Job 22:23
13412.text: If you return to the Almighty, you will be restored; If you remove unrighteousness from your tent,

13413.label: Job 22:24
13413.text: If you would throw your gold into the dustAnd the gold of Oʹphir into the rocky ravines,

13414.label: Job 22:25
13414.text: Then the Almighty will become your gold, And he will be your choicest silver.

13415.label: Job 22:26
13415.text: For then your delight will be in the Almighty,And you will lift up your face to God.

13416.label: Job 22:27
13416.text: You will entreat him, and he will hear you;And your vows you will pay.

13417.label: Job 22:28
13417.text: Whatever you decide to do will succeed,And light will shine upon your path.

13418.label: Job 22:29
13418.text: For you will be humiliated when you speak arrogantly,But he will save the humble.

13419.label: Job 22:30
13419.text: He will rescue those who are innocent;So if your hands are clean, you will certainly be rescued.”

13421.label: Job 23:2
13421.text: “Even today I will complain stubbornly; My strength is exhausted because of my sighing.

13422.label: Job 23:3
13422.text: If only I knew where to find God! I would go to his place of dwelling.

13423.label: Job 23:4
13423.text: I would present my case before himAnd fill my mouth with arguments;

13424.label: Job 23:5
13424.text: I would learn how he would answer meAnd take note of what he says to me.

13425.label: Job 23:6
13425.text: Would he contend with me using his great power? No, surely he would give me a hearing.

13426.label: Job 23:7
13426.text: There the upright one could set matters straight with him,And I would be acquitted once and for all by my Judge.

13427.label: Job 23:8
13427.text: But if I go east, he is not there;And I return and I cannot find him.

13428.label: Job 23:9
13428.text: When he is working on the left, I cannot look upon him;Then he turns to the right, but I still do not see him.

13429.label: Job 23:10
13429.text: But he knows the path I have taken. After he has tested me, I will come out as pure gold.

13430.label: Job 23:11
13430.text: My feet have closely followed his footsteps;I have kept to his way without deviating.

13431.label: Job 23:12
13431.text: I have not departed from the commandment of his lips. I have treasured up his sayings even more than what was required of me.

13432.label: Job 23:13
13432.text: When he is determined, who can resist him? When he wants to do something, he does it.

13433.label: Job 23:14
13433.text: For he will carry out completely what has been determined for me,And he has many such things in store.

13434.label: Job 23:15
13434.text: That is why I am anxious because of him;When I think about him, my fear grows.

13435.label: Job 23:16
13435.text: God has made me fainthearted,And the Almighty has made me afraid.

13436.label: Job 23:17
13436.text: But I have not yet been silenced by the darknessNor by the gloom that has covered my face.

13437.label: Job 24:1
13437.text: “Why does the Almighty not set a time? Why do those who know him not see his day?

13438.label: Job 24:2
13438.text: People move boundary markers; They carry off flocks for their own pasture.

13439.label: Job 24:3
13439.text: They drive away the donkey of fatherless childrenAnd seize the widow’s bull as security for a loan.

13440.label: Job 24:4
13440.text: They force the poor off the road;The helpless of the earth must hide from them.

13441.label: Job 24:5
13441.text: The poor forage for food like wild donkeys in the wilderness;They seek food in the desert for their children.

13442.label: Job 24:6
13442.text: They must harvest in another’s field And glean from the vineyard of the wicked.

13443.label: Job 24:7
13443.text: They spend the night naked, without clothing; They have no covering for the cold.

13444.label: Job 24:8
13444.text: They are drenched by the mountain rains;They cling to the rocks for lack of shelter.

13445.label: Job 24:9
13445.text: The fatherless child is snatched away from the breast; And the garments of the poor are taken as security for a loan,

13446.label: Job 24:10
13446.text: Forcing them to go about naked, without clothing,And hungry, as they carry the sheaves of grain.

13447.label: Job 24:11
13447.text: They toil among the terrace walls in the heat of the day; They tread the winepresses, yet they go thirsty.

13448.label: Job 24:12
13448.text: The dying keep groaning in the city;The fatally wounded cry for help, But God does not regard this as improper.

13449.label: Job 24:13
13449.text: There are those who rebel against light; They do not recognize its ways,And they do not follow its paths.

13450.label: Job 24:14
13450.text: The murderer rises at daybreak;He slays the helpless and the poor, While at night he engages in theft.

13451.label: Job 24:15
13451.text: The eye of the adulterer waits for the twilight, Saying, ‘No one will see me!’ And he covers his face.

13452.label: Job 24:16
13452.text: In the darkness they break into houses;By day they shut themselves in. They are strangers to the light.

13453.label: Job 24:17
13453.text: For morning is the same as deep darkness for them;They are familiar with the terrors of deep darkness.

13454.label: Job 24:18
13454.text: But they are swiftly carried away by the waters. Their portion of the land will be cursed. They will not return to their vineyards.

13455.label: Job 24:19
13455.text: Just as drought and heat take away the melted snow,The Grave takes away those who have sinned!

13456.label: Job 24:20
13456.text: His mother will forget him; the maggot will feast on him. He will be remembered no more. And unrighteousness will be broken just like a tree.

13457.label: Job 24:21
13457.text: He preys on the barren woman,And mistreats the widow.

13458.label: Job 24:22
13458.text: God will use his strength to do away with the powerful;Though they may rise up, they have no assurance of life.

13459.label: Job 24:23
13459.text: God lets them become confident and secure, But his eyes are on everything they do.

13460.label: Job 24:24
13460.text: They are exalted for a little while, then they are no more. They are brought low and gathered like everyone else;They are cut off like heads of grain.

13461.label: Job 24:25
13461.text: Now who can prove me a liarOr refute my word?”

13462.label: Job 25:1
13462.text: Bilʹdad the Shuʹhite said in reply:

13463.label: Job 25:2
13463.text: “Rulership and fearsome might are his;He establishes peace in heaven.

13464.label: Job 25:3
13464.text: Can his troops be numbered? Upon whom does his light not rise?

13465.label: Job 25:4
13465.text: So how can mortal man be righteous before God, Or how can one born of a woman be innocent?

13466.label: Job 25:5
13466.text: Even the moon is not brightAnd the stars are not pure in his eyes,

13467.label: Job 25:6
13467.text: How much less so mortal man, who is a maggot,And a son of man, who is a worm!”

13469.label: Job 26:2
13469.text: “How you have helped the one with no power! How you have saved the arm that has no strength!

13470.label: Job 26:3
13470.text: What great advice you have given to the one lacking wisdom! How freely you have revealed your practical wisdom!

13471.label: Job 26:4
13471.text: To whom are you trying to speak,And who inspired you to say such things?

13472.label: Job 26:5
13472.text: Those who are powerless in death tremble;They are even lower than the waters and their inhabitants.

13473.label: Job 26:6
13473.text: The Grave is naked in front of God, And the place of destruction lies uncovered.

13474.label: Job 26:7
13474.text: He stretches out the northern sky over empty space, Suspending the earth upon nothing;

13475.label: Job 26:8
13475.text: He wraps up the waters in his clouds, So that the clouds do not burst under their weight;

13476.label: Job 26:9
13476.text: He shuts off the view of his throne,Spreading out his cloud over it.

13477.label: Job 26:10
13477.text: He marks out the horizon on the surface of the waters; He makes a boundary between light and darkness.

13478.label: Job 26:11
13478.text: The very pillars of heaven shake;They are stunned by his rebuke.

13479.label: Job 26:12
13479.text: He stirs up the sea with his power, And by his understanding he breaks the sea monster to pieces.

13480.label: Job 26:13
13480.text: With his breath he makes the skies clear;His hand pierces the elusive serpent.

13481.label: Job 26:14
13481.text: Look! These are just the fringes of his ways; Only a faint whisper has been heard of him! So who can understand his mighty thunder?”

13483.label: Job 27:2
13483.text: “As surely as God lives, who has deprived me of justice, As the Almighty lives, who has made me bitter,

13484.label: Job 27:3
13484.text: As long as my breath is within meAnd spirit from God is in my nostrils,

13485.label: Job 27:4
13485.text: My lips will not speak unrighteousness;Nor will my tongue mutter deceit!

13486.label: Job 27:5
13486.text: It is unthinkable for me to declare you men righteous! Until I die, I will not renounce my integrity!

13487.label: Job 27:6
13487.text: I will maintain my righteousness and never let it go; My heart will not condemn me as long as I live.

13488.label: Job 27:7
13488.text: May my enemy become like the wicked,Those assaulting me like the unrighteous.

13489.label: Job 27:8
13489.text: For what hope does the godless man have when he is destroyed, When God takes away his life?

13490.label: Job 27:9
13490.text: Will God hear his outcryWhen distress comes upon him?

13491.label: Job 27:10
13491.text: Or will he find delight in the Almighty? Will he call on God at all times?

13492.label: Job 27:11
13492.text: I will teach you about the power of God;I will not hide anything about the Almighty.

13493.label: Job 27:12
13493.text: Look! If you have all seen visions,Why are your speeches completely empty?

13494.label: Job 27:13
13494.text: This is the wicked man’s share from God, The inheritance that tyrants receive from the Almighty.

13495.label: Job 27:14
13495.text: If his sons become many, they will fall by the sword, And his descendants will not have enough food.

13496.label: Job 27:15
13496.text: Those who survive him will be buried by the plague,And their widows will not weep for them.

13497.label: Job 27:16
13497.text: Even if he piles up silver like the dustAnd stores up fine clothing like the clay,

13498.label: Job 27:17
13498.text: Though he may gather it,The righteous man will wear it, And the innocent will divide up his silver.

13499.label: Job 27:18
13499.text: The house he builds is as fragile as a moth’s cocoon,Like a shelter made by a watchman.

13500.label: Job 27:19
13500.text: He will go to bed rich but will gather nothing;When he opens his eyes, nothing will be there.

13501.label: Job 27:20
13501.text: Terror overtakes him like a flood;A storm snatches him away by night.

13502.label: Job 27:21
13502.text: An east wind will carry him off, and he will be gone;It sweeps him away from his place.

13503.label: Job 27:22
13503.text: It will hurl itself at him without pity As he desperately tries to flee from its force.

13504.label: Job 27:23
13504.text: It claps its hands at himAnd whistles at him from its place.

13505.label: Job 28:1
13505.text: “There is a place to mine silverAnd a place for gold that they refine;

13506.label: Job 28:2
13506.text: Iron is taken from the ground,And copper is smelted from rocks.

13507.label: Job 28:3
13507.text: Man conquers the darkness;He probes to the limit in the gloom and darkness,Searching for ore.

13508.label: Job 28:4
13508.text: He sinks a shaft far from where people reside,In forgotten places, far from where people walk;Some men descend and swing suspended.

13509.label: Job 28:5
13509.text: Food grows on top of the earth;But below, there is an upheaval as if by fire.

13510.label: Job 28:6
13510.text: There in the stones is sapphire,And the dust contains gold.

13511.label: Job 28:7
13511.text: No bird of prey knows the path to it;The eye of a black kite has not seen it.

13512.label: Job 28:8
13512.text: No majestic beasts have trodden on it;The young lion has not prowled there.

13513.label: Job 28:9
13513.text: Man strikes the flinty rock with his hand;He overturns the mountains at their foundation.

13514.label: Job 28:10
13514.text: He cuts water channels in the rock;His eyes spot every precious thing.

13515.label: Job 28:11
13515.text: He dams up the sources of riversAnd brings what was hidden to the light.

13516.label: Job 28:12
13516.text: But wisdom—where can it be found, And where is the source of understanding?

13517.label: Job 28:13
13517.text: No man recognizes its value, And it cannot be found in the land of the living.

13518.label: Job 28:14
13518.text: The deep waters say, ‘It is not in me!’ And the sea says, ‘It is not with me!’

13519.label: Job 28:15
13519.text: It cannot be bought with pure gold;Nor can silver be weighed out in exchange for it.

13520.label: Job 28:16
13520.text: It cannot be bought with gold of Oʹphir Nor with rare onyx and sapphire.
