13521.label: Job 28:17
13521.text: Gold and glass cannot be compared to it;Nor can a vessel of fine gold be exchanged for it.

13522.label: Job 28:18
13522.text: Coral and crystal are not worthy of mention, For a bagful of wisdom is worth more than one full of pearls.

13523.label: Job 28:19
13523.text: The topaz of Cush cannot be compared to it;It cannot be purchased even with pure gold.

13524.label: Job 28:20
13524.text: But from where does wisdom come,And where is the source of understanding?

13525.label: Job 28:21
13525.text: It has been hidden from the eyes of every living thing And concealed from the birds of the heavens.

13526.label: Job 28:22
13526.text: Destruction and death say,‘Our ears have heard only a report of it.’

13527.label: Job 28:23
13527.text: God understands the way to find it;He alone knows where it resides,

13528.label: Job 28:24
13528.text: For he looks to the ends of the earth,And he sees everything under the heavens.

13529.label: Job 28:25
13529.text: When he set the force of the wind And measured out the waters,

13530.label: Job 28:26
13530.text: When he made a regulation for the rain And a path for the thunderous storm cloud,

13531.label: Job 28:27
13531.text: Then he saw wisdom and explained it;He established and tested it.

13532.label: Job 28:28
13532.text: And he said to man: ‘Look! The fear of Jehovah—that is wisdom, And to turn away from bad is understanding.’”

13534.label: Job 29:2
13534.text: “If only I were in the months gone by,In the days when God was watching over me,

13535.label: Job 29:3
13535.text: When he caused his lamp to shine upon my head,When I walked through darkness by his light,

13536.label: Job 29:4
13536.text: When I was in my prime,When God’s friendship was felt in my tent,

13537.label: Job 29:5
13537.text: When the Almighty was still with me,When my children were all around me,

13538.label: Job 29:6
13538.text: When my steps were awash in butter,And the rocks poured out streams of oil for me.

13539.label: Job 29:7
13539.text: When I used to go out to the city gate And take my seat in the public square,

13540.label: Job 29:8
13540.text: The young men would see me and step aside, And even the old men would rise and remain standing.

13541.label: Job 29:9
13541.text: Princes refrained from speaking;They would put their hand over their mouth.

13542.label: Job 29:10
13542.text: The voices of the prominent men were silenced;Their tongue was stuck to the roof of their mouth.

13543.label: Job 29:11
13543.text: Whoever heard me would speak well of me,And those who saw me would testify for me.

13544.label: Job 29:12
13544.text: For I would rescue the poor who cried for help, Along with the fatherless child and anyone who had no helper.

13545.label: Job 29:13
13545.text: The one about to perish would bless me, And I made the heart of the widow rejoice.

13546.label: Job 29:14
13546.text: I put on righteousness as my clothing;My justice was like a robe and a turban.

13547.label: Job 29:15
13547.text: I became eyes to the blindAnd feet to the lame.

13548.label: Job 29:16
13548.text: I was a father to the poor; I would investigate the legal case of those I did not know.

13549.label: Job 29:17
13549.text: I would break the jaws of the wrongdoer And tear the prey away from his teeth.

13550.label: Job 29:18
13550.text: I used to say, ‘I will die in my own home, And my days will be as numerous as the grains of sand.

13551.label: Job 29:19
13551.text: My roots will spread out into the waters,And dew will stay all night on my branches.

13552.label: Job 29:20
13552.text: My glory is constantly renewed,And the bow in my hand will keep shooting.’

13553.label: Job 29:21
13553.text: People would listen expectantly,Waiting in silence for my advice.

13554.label: Job 29:22
13554.text: After I had spoken, they had nothing more to say;My words would fall gently on their ears.

13555.label: Job 29:23
13555.text: They waited for me as for the rain;They opened their mouth wide as for the spring rain.

13556.label: Job 29:24
13556.text: When I smiled at them, they could hardly believe it;The light of my face would reassure them.

13557.label: Job 29:25
13557.text: I gave them direction as their head,And I lived like a king among his troops, Like one who comforts the mourners.

13558.label: Job 30:1
13558.text: “Now they laugh at me —Men younger than I am,Whose fathers I would have refusedTo put with the dogs that guarded my flock.

13559.label: Job 30:2
13559.text: Of what use was the power of their hands to me? Their vigor has perished.

13560.label: Job 30:3
13560.text: They are worn out from want and hunger;They gnaw at the parched groundThat was already ruined and desolated.

13561.label: Job 30:4
13561.text: They gather the salt herb from the bushes;Their food is the root of broom trees.

13562.label: Job 30:5
13562.text: They are driven out of the community; People shout at them as they would at a thief.

13563.label: Job 30:6
13563.text: They live on the slopes of ravines, In holes in the ground and in the rocks.

13564.label: Job 30:7
13564.text: From the bushes they cry outAnd huddle together among the nettles.

13565.label: Job 30:8
13565.text: As sons of the senseless and the nameless ones,They have been driven out of the land.

13566.label: Job 30:9
13566.text: But now they mock me even in their songs; I have become an object of scorn to them.

13567.label: Job 30:10
13567.text: They detest me and keep their distance from me; They do not hesitate to spit in my face.

13568.label: Job 30:11
13568.text: Because God has disarmed me and humbled me,They throw off all restraint in my presence.

13569.label: Job 30:12
13569.text: On my right they rise up like a mob;They put me to flightAnd put up barriers of destruction in my path.

13570.label: Job 30:13
13570.text: They tear up my roadwaysAnd make my calamity worse, Without anyone to stop them.

13571.label: Job 30:14
13571.text: They come as if through a wide breach in the wall;They roll in amid the devastation.

13572.label: Job 30:15
13572.text: Terror overwhelms me;My dignity is driven away like the wind,And my salvation vanishes like a cloud.

13573.label: Job 30:16
13573.text: Now my life ebbs from me; Days of affliction take hold of me.

13574.label: Job 30:17
13574.text: Aching pierces my bones at night; The gnawing pain never stops.

13575.label: Job 30:18
13575.text: With great force my garment is disfigured; Like the collar of my garment, it chokes me.

13576.label: Job 30:19
13576.text: God has thrown me down into the mud;I am reduced to dust and ashes.

13577.label: Job 30:20
13577.text: I cry to you for help, but you do not answer me; I stand up, but you just look at me.

13578.label: Job 30:21
13578.text: You have cruelly turned against me; With the full might of your hand, you assault me.

13579.label: Job 30:22
13579.text: You pick me up and carry me off with the wind;Then you toss me about in the storm.

13580.label: Job 30:23
13580.text: For I know that you will bring me down to death,To the house where everyone living will meet.

13581.label: Job 30:24
13581.text: But no one would strike at a broken man As he cries for help during his time of disaster.

13582.label: Job 30:25
13582.text: Have I not wept for those who have fallen on hard times? Have I not grieved for the poor?

13583.label: Job 30:26
13583.text: Although I hoped for good, bad came;I expected the light, but darkness came.

13584.label: Job 30:27
13584.text: The churning inside me did not stop;Days of affliction confronted me.

13585.label: Job 30:28
13585.text: I walk about gloomy; there is no sunlight. In the assembly, I rise and cry for help.

13586.label: Job 30:29
13586.text: I have become a brother to jackalsAnd a companion to the daughters of the ostrich.

13587.label: Job 30:30
13587.text: My skin has blackened and fallen off; My bones burn from the heat.

13588.label: Job 30:31
13588.text: My harp is used only for mourning,And my flute for the sound of weeping.

13589.label: Job 31:1
13589.text: “I have made a covenant with my eyes. So how could I show improper attention to a virgin?

13590.label: Job 31:2
13590.text: What, then, would be my share from God above,What inheritance from the Almighty on high?

13591.label: Job 31:3
13591.text: Does not disaster await the wrongdoerAnd calamity those doing what is harmful?

13592.label: Job 31:4
13592.text: Does he not see my ways And count all my steps?

13593.label: Job 31:5
13593.text: Have I ever walked in untruth? Has my foot hurried to deceive?

13594.label: Job 31:6
13594.text: Let God weigh me with accurate scales; Then he will recognize my integrity.

13595.label: Job 31:7
13595.text: If my footsteps deviate from the way Or my heart has followed after my eyes Or my hands have been defiled,

13596.label: Job 31:8
13596.text: Then let me sow seed and someone else eat, And let what I plant be uprooted.

13597.label: Job 31:9
13597.text: If my heart has been enticed by a woman And I have lain in wait at my neighbor’s door,

13598.label: Job 31:10
13598.text: Then let my wife grind grain for another man,And let other men have sexual relations with her.

13599.label: Job 31:11
13599.text: For that would be shameful conduct,An error deserving punishment by the judges.

13600.label: Job 31:12
13600.text: It would be a fire that would devour and destroy, Consuming even the roots of all my produce.

13601.label: Job 31:13
13601.text: If I denied justice to my male or female servantsWhen they had a complaint against me,

13602.label: Job 31:14
13602.text: What can I do when God confronts me? What can I answer him when he calls for an accounting?

13603.label: Job 31:15
13603.text: Did not the One who made me in the womb also make them? Was it not the same One who formed us before our birth?

13604.label: Job 31:16
13604.text: If I refused to give the poor what they desired Or saddened the eyes of the widow;

13605.label: Job 31:17
13605.text: If I ate my portion of food aloneWithout sharing it with the orphans;

13606.label: Job 31:18
13606.text: (For from my youth the orphan grew up with me as though I were his father,And I have been a guide for the widow from childhood. )

13607.label: Job 31:19
13607.text: If I saw anyone perishing for lack of clothingOr a poor man with nothing to cover himself;

13608.label: Job 31:20
13608.text: If he did not bless me As he warmed himself with the wool of my sheep;

13609.label: Job 31:21
13609.text: If I shook my fist against the orphan When he needed my assistance in the city gate;

13610.label: Job 31:22
13610.text: Then let my arm fall from my shoulder,And let my arm be broken at the elbow.

13611.label: Job 31:23
13611.text: For I dreaded disaster from God,And I could not stand before his dignity.

13612.label: Job 31:24
13612.text: If I put my confidence in goldOr said to fine gold, ‘You are my security!’

13613.label: Job 31:25
13613.text: If I found my joy in my great wealth Because of the many possessions I acquired;

13614.label: Job 31:26
13614.text: If I saw the sun shiningOr the moon moving in its splendor;

13615.label: Job 31:27
13615.text: And my heart was secretly enticed,And my mouth kissed my hand in worship of them;

13616.label: Job 31:28
13616.text: Then that would be an error deserving punishment by the judges,For I would have denied the true God above.

13617.label: Job 31:29
13617.text: Have I ever rejoiced over the destruction of my enemy Or gloated because evil befell him?

13618.label: Job 31:30
13618.text: I never allowed my mouth to sinBy asking for his life in an oath.

13619.label: Job 31:31
13619.text: Have the men of my tent not said,‘Who can find anyone who has not been satisfied with his food?’

13620.label: Job 31:32
13620.text: No stranger had to spend the night outside; I opened my doors to the traveler.

13621.label: Job 31:33
13621.text: Have I ever tried to cover over my transgressions, like other men, By hiding my error in the pocket of my garment?

13622.label: Job 31:34
13622.text: Have I been in fear of the reaction of the multitude,Or have I been terrified by the contempt of other families,Making me silent and afraid to go outside?

13623.label: Job 31:35
13623.text: If only someone would listen to me! I would sign my name to what I have said. Let the Almighty answer me! If only my accuser had written out the charges in a document!

13624.label: Job 31:36
13624.text: I would carry it on my shoulder,And I would bind it around my head like a crown.

13625.label: Job 31:37
13625.text: I would give him an accounting for every step I took;I would approach him confidently, like a prince.

13626.label: Job 31:38
13626.text: If my own ground would cry out against meAnd its furrows would weep together;

13627.label: Job 31:39
13627.text: If I have eaten its fruitage without payment, Or if I have caused its owners to despair;

13628.label: Job 31:40
13628.text: Then let thorns sprout for me instead of wheatAnd foul-smelling weeds instead of barley.” The words of Job end here.

13629.label: Job 32:1
13629.text: So these three men stopped trying to answer Job, because he was convinced of his own righteousness.

13630.label: Job 32:2
13630.text: But E·liʹhu the son of Barʹa·chel the Buzʹite of the family of Ram had become very angry. His anger blazed against Job for trying to prove himself right rather than God.

13631.label: Job 32:3
13631.text: He was also very angry with Job’s three companions because they could not find an answer but had declared God wicked.

13632.label: Job 32:4
13632.text: E·liʹhu had been waiting to respond to Job, because they were older than he was.

13633.label: Job 32:5
13633.text: When E·liʹhu saw that the three men had nothing to say in answer, his anger flared up.

13634.label: Job 32:6
13634.text: So E·liʹhu the son of Barʹa·chel the Buzʹite began to speak, saying: “I am young And you men are aged. So I respectfully held back, And I dared not tell you what I know.

13635.label: Job 32:7
13635.text: I thought, ‘Let age speak,And let a multitude of years declare wisdom.’

13636.label: Job 32:8
13636.text: But it is the spirit in people,The breath of the Almighty, that gives them understanding.

13637.label: Job 32:9
13637.text: Age alone does not make one wise,Nor is it only old men who understand what is right.

13638.label: Job 32:10
13638.text: So I say, ‘Listen to me,And I will also tell you what I know.’

13639.label: Job 32:11
13639.text: Look! I have waited for your words;I kept listening to your reasoning As you searched for things to say.

13640.label: Job 32:12
13640.text: I paid close attention to you,But none of you could prove Job wrong Or answer his arguments.

13641.label: Job 32:13
13641.text: So do not say, ‘We have found wisdom;It is God who refutes him, not a man.’

13642.label: Job 32:14
13642.text: He did not direct his words against me,So I will not reply to him with your arguments.

13643.label: Job 32:15
13643.text: They are dismayed, they have no more answers;They have nothing left to say.

13644.label: Job 32:16
13644.text: I have waited, but they do not continue speaking;They just stand there, with no further answer.

13645.label: Job 32:17
13645.text: So I too will give an answer;I too will tell what I know,

13646.label: Job 32:18
13646.text: For I am full of words;The spirit within me compels me.

13647.label: Job 32:19
13647.text: My insides are like wine that has no vent,Like new wineskins ready to burst.

13648.label: Job 32:20
13648.text: Let me speak so that I can find relief! I will open my lips and give an answer.

13649.label: Job 32:21
13649.text: I will not show partiality to anyone; Nor will I flatter any human,

13650.label: Job 32:22
13650.text: For I do not know how to flatter;If I did, my Maker would quickly do away with me.

13651.label: Job 33:1
13651.text: “But now, Job, please hear my words;Listen to everything I say.

13652.label: Job 33:2
13652.text: Look, please! I must open my mouth;My tongue must speak.

13653.label: Job 33:3
13653.text: My words declare the uprightness of my heart, And my lips sincerely tell what I know.

13654.label: Job 33:4
13654.text: God’s own spirit made me, And the Almighty’s own breath brought me to life.

13655.label: Job 33:5
13655.text: Reply to me if you are able;Present your arguments before me; take your position.

13656.label: Job 33:6
13656.text: Look! I am just like you before the true God;From the clay I too was shaped.

13657.label: Job 33:7
13657.text: So no fear of me should terrify you,And no pressure from me should overwhelm you.

13658.label: Job 33:8
13658.text: But you said in my hearing,Yes, I kept hearing these words,

13659.label: Job 33:9
13659.text: ‘I am pure, without transgression; I am clean, without error.

13660.label: Job 33:10
13660.text: But God finds reasons to oppose me;He considers me his enemy.

13661.label: Job 33:11
13661.text: He puts my feet in stocks;He scrutinizes all my paths.’

13662.label: Job 33:12
13662.text: But you are not right in saying this, so I will answer you: God is far greater than mortal man.

13663.label: Job 33:13
13663.text: Why do you complain against Him? Is it because he did not answer all your words?

13664.label: Job 33:14
13664.text: For God speaks once and a second time,But no one pays attention,

13665.label: Job 33:15
13665.text: In a dream, a vision of the night, When deep sleep falls upon peopleWhile they sleep in their beds.

13666.label: Job 33:16
13666.text: Then he uncovers their ears And impresses his instruction upon them,

13667.label: Job 33:17
13667.text: To turn a person away from wrongdoing And to protect a man from pride.

13668.label: Job 33:18
13668.text: God spares his soul from the pit, His life from perishing by the sword.

13669.label: Job 33:19
13669.text: A person is also reproved by pain on his bedAnd by the constant distress of his bones,

13670.label: Job 33:20
13670.text: So that his very being loathes bread,And he rejects even fine food.

13671.label: Job 33:21
13671.text: His flesh wastes away from sight,And his bones that were hidden now protrude.

13672.label: Job 33:22
13672.text: His soul draws near to the pit; His life to those who bring death.

13673.label: Job 33:23
13673.text: If there is a messenger for him,One advocate out of a thousand,To tell to man what is upright,

13674.label: Job 33:24
13674.text: Then God shows him favor and says,‘Spare him from going down into the pit! I have found a ransom!

13675.label: Job 33:25
13675.text: Let his flesh become fresher than in youth; Let him return to the days of his youthful vigor.’

13676.label: Job 33:26
13676.text: He will entreat God, who will accept him,And he will see His face with shouts of joy,And He will restore His righteousness to mortal man.

13677.label: Job 33:27
13677.text: That person will declare to men,‘I have sinned and distorted what is right,But I did not receive what I deserved.

13678.label: Job 33:28
13678.text: He has redeemed my soul from going into the pit, And my life will see the light.’

13679.label: Job 33:29
13679.text: Indeed, God does all these thingsTwice, three times, for a man,

13680.label: Job 33:30
13680.text: To bring him back from the pit, So that he may be enlightened with the light of life.

13681.label: Job 33:31
13681.text: Pay attention, Job! Listen to me! Keep silent, and I will continue speaking.

13682.label: Job 33:32
13682.text: If you have something to say, reply to me. Speak, for I want to prove you right.

13683.label: Job 33:33
13683.text: If you have nothing to say, you should listen to me;Keep silent, and I will teach you wisdom.”

13684.label: Job 34:1
13684.text: So E·liʹhu continued to say in reply:

13685.label: Job 34:2
13685.text: “Listen to my words, you who are wise;Hear me, you who know so much.

13686.label: Job 34:3
13686.text: For the ear tests wordsJust as the tongue tastes food.

13687.label: Job 34:4
13687.text: Let us evaluate for ourselves what is right;Let us decide among ourselves what is good.

13688.label: Job 34:5
13688.text: For Job has said, ‘I am in the right, But God has denied me justice.

13689.label: Job 34:6
13689.text: Would I lie about what my own judgment should be? My wound is incurable, though there is no transgression.’

13690.label: Job 34:7
13690.text: What other man is like Job,Who drinks up derision like water?

13691.label: Job 34:8
13691.text: He is in company with wrongdoersAnd in association with wicked men.

13692.label: Job 34:9
13692.text: For he has said, ‘A man does not benefitFrom trying to please God.’

13693.label: Job 34:10
13693.text: So listen to me, you men of understanding: It is unthinkable for the true God to act wickedly, For the Almighty to do wrong!

13694.label: Job 34:11
13694.text: For he will reward a man according to what he does And bring upon him the consequences of his ways.

13695.label: Job 34:12
13695.text: For a certainty, God does not act wickedly; The Almighty does not pervert justice.

13696.label: Job 34:13
13696.text: Who put him in charge of the earth,And who appointed him over the whole world?

13697.label: Job 34:14
13697.text: If he fixes his attention on them,If he gathers their spirit and breath to himself,

13698.label: Job 34:15
13698.text: All humans would perish together,And mankind would return to the dust.

13699.label: Job 34:16
13699.text: So if you have understanding, pay attention to this;Listen carefully to what I say.

13700.label: Job 34:17
13700.text: Should someone who hates justice be in control,Or would you condemn a powerful one who is righteous?

13701.label: Job 34:18
13701.text: Would you say to a king, ‘You are good for nothing,’ Or to nobles, ‘You are wicked’?

13702.label: Job 34:19
13702.text: There is One who does not show partiality to princesAnd who does not favor the rich over the poor, For they are all the work of his hands.

13703.label: Job 34:20
13703.text: They may die suddenly, in the middle of the night; They shake violently and pass away;Even the powerful are removed, but not by human hands.

13704.label: Job 34:21
13704.text: For God’s eyes are upon the ways of a man, And He sees all his steps.

13705.label: Job 34:22
13705.text: There is no darkness or deep shadowWhere wrongdoers can conceal themselves.

13706.label: Job 34:23
13706.text: For God has not set an appointed time for any manTo appear before him in judgment.

13707.label: Job 34:24
13707.text: He breaks the powerful without needing to investigateAnd sets up others in their place.

13708.label: Job 34:25
13708.text: For he knows what they are doing; He overthrows them during the night, and they are crushed.

13709.label: Job 34:26
13709.text: He strikes them for their wickedness,In a place where all can see,

13710.label: Job 34:27
13710.text: Because they have turned away from following him And have no regard for any of his ways;

13711.label: Job 34:28
13711.text: They cause the poor to cry out to him,So that he hears the outcry of the helpless.

13712.label: Job 34:29
13712.text: When God remains silent, who can condemn him? When he hides his face, who can see him? Whether toward a nation or a man, the result is the same,

13713.label: Job 34:30
13713.text: So that a godless person may not rule Or lay snares for the people.

13714.label: Job 34:31
13714.text: For will anyone say to God,‘I have been punished, although I have committed no offense;

13715.label: Job 34:32
13715.text: Teach me what I have failed to see;If I have done anything wrong, I will not do it again’?

13716.label: Job 34:33
13716.text: Should he reward you on your terms when you reject his judgment? You must decide, not I. So tell me what you know so well.

13717.label: Job 34:34
13717.text: Men of understanding will say to me—Any wise man who hears me—

13718.label: Job 34:35
13718.text: ‘Job speaks without knowledge, And his words lack insight.’

13719.label: Job 34:36
13719.text: Let Job be tested to the limitBecause his replies are like those of wicked men!

13720.label: Job 34:37
13720.text: He adds rebellion to his sin; He scornfully claps his hands before usAnd multiplies his words against the true God!”

13722.label: Job 35:2
13722.text: “Are you so convinced that you are right that you would say,‘I am more righteous than God’?

13723.label: Job 35:3
13723.text: For you say, ‘What does it matter to you? Am I better off than if I had sinned?’

13724.label: Job 35:4
13724.text: I will reply to youAnd to your companions with you.

13725.label: Job 35:5
13725.text: Look up to heaven and see,Observe the clouds, which are high above you.

13726.label: Job 35:6
13726.text: If you sin, how do you hurt him? If your transgressions multiply, what do you do to him?

13727.label: Job 35:7
13727.text: If you are righteous, what do you give him;What does he receive from you?

13728.label: Job 35:8
13728.text: Your wickedness affects only a human like yourself,And your righteousness, a son of man.

13729.label: Job 35:9
13729.text: People cry out when under great oppression;They cry for relief from the domination of the powerful.

13730.label: Job 35:10
13730.text: But no one says, ‘Where is God, my Grand Maker, The one causing songs to be sung in the night?’

13731.label: Job 35:11
13731.text: He teaches us more than the beasts of the earth, And he makes us wiser than the birds of the heavens.

13732.label: Job 35:12
13732.text: People cry out, but he does not answer, Because of the pride of the wicked.

13733.label: Job 35:13
13733.text: Surely God does not hear an empty cry; The Almighty does not pay attention to it.

13734.label: Job 35:14
13734.text: How much less, then, when you complain that you do not see him! Your legal case is before him, so you should wait anxiously for him.

13735.label: Job 35:15
13735.text: For he has not angrily called for an accounting;Nor has he taken note of your extreme rashness.

13736.label: Job 35:16
13736.text: Job opens his mouth wide in vain;He multiplies words without knowledge.”

13738.label: Job 36:2
13738.text: “Be patient with me a little longer while I explain,For I still have words to speak on God’s behalf.

13739.label: Job 36:3
13739.text: I will speak comprehensively about what I know,And I will ascribe righteousness to my Maker.

13740.label: Job 36:4
13740.text: Truly my words are not false;The One perfect in knowledge is here before you.

13741.label: Job 36:5
13741.text: Indeed, God is mighty and rejects no one;He is great in his power of understanding.

13742.label: Job 36:6
13742.text: He will not preserve the lives of the wicked, But he gives justice to the afflicted.

13743.label: Job 36:7
13743.text: He does not take his eyes off the righteous; He enthrones them with kings, and they are exalted forever.

13744.label: Job 36:8
13744.text: But if they are bound in shacklesAnd caught in ropes of affliction,

13745.label: Job 36:9
13745.text: He reveals to them what they have done,Their transgressions caused by their pride.

13746.label: Job 36:10
13746.text: He opens their ears to correctionAnd tells them to turn away from wrongdoing.

13747.label: Job 36:11
13747.text: If they obey and serve him,They will live out their days in prosperity,And their years will be pleasant.

13748.label: Job 36:12
13748.text: But if they do not obey, they will perish by the sword And die without knowledge.

13749.label: Job 36:13
13749.text: The godless at heart will harbor resentment. They do not cry for help even when he binds them.

13750.label: Job 36:14
13750.text: They die while still young, Spending their life among male temple prostitutes.

13751.label: Job 36:15
13751.text: But God rescues the afflicted during their affliction;He opens their ear when they are oppressed.

13752.label: Job 36:16
13752.text: He draws you away from the brink of distress To a broad space, free of restriction, With rich food on your table as consolation.

13753.label: Job 36:17
13753.text: Then you will be satisfied with the judgment on the wicked, When judgment is rendered and justice is upheld.

13754.label: Job 36:18
13754.text: But take care that rage does not lead you into spitefulness, And do not let a large bribe lead you astray.

13755.label: Job 36:19
13755.text: Would your cry for helpOr any of your strenuous efforts keep you from distress?

13756.label: Job 36:20
13756.text: Do not long for the night,When people vanish from their place.

13757.label: Job 36:21
13757.text: Beware that you do not turn to wrongdoing,Choosing this instead of affliction.

13758.label: Job 36:22
13758.text: Look! God is exalted in his power;What instructor is like him?

13759.label: Job 36:23
13759.text: Who has directed his way Or said to him, ‘What you have done is wrong’?

13760.label: Job 36:24
13760.text: Remember to magnify his activity, Of which men have sung.

13761.label: Job 36:25
13761.text: All mankind has seen it,Mortal man looks on from a distance.

13762.label: Job 36:26
13762.text: Yes, God is greater than we can know; The number of his years is beyond comprehension.

13763.label: Job 36:27
13763.text: He draws up the drops of water; They condense into rain from his mist;

13764.label: Job 36:28
13764.text: Then the clouds pour it down; They shower down upon mankind.

13765.label: Job 36:29
13765.text: Can anyone understand the layers of clouds,The thundering from his tent?

13766.label: Job 36:30
13766.text: See how he spreads his lightning over itAnd covers the depths of the sea.

13767.label: Job 36:31
13767.text: By these he sustains the peoples;He gives them food in abundance.

13768.label: Job 36:32
13768.text: With his hands he covers the lightning,And he directs it against its target.

13769.label: Job 36:33
13769.text: His thunder tells about him,Even the livestock tell who is coming.

13770.label: Job 37:1
13770.text: “At this my heart poundsAnd leaps from its place.

13771.label: Job 37:2
13771.text: Listen carefully to the rumbling of his voiceAnd the thunder that comes from his mouth.

13772.label: Job 37:3
13772.text: He unleashes it under the entire heavensAnd sends his lightning to the ends of the earth.

13773.label: Job 37:4
13773.text: After that is a roaring sound;He thunders with a majestic voice, And he does not hold it back when his voice is heard.

13774.label: Job 37:5
13774.text: God thunders with his voice in a wonderful way;He does great things that are beyond our understanding.

13775.label: Job 37:6
13775.text: For he says to the snow, ‘Fall to the earth,’ And to the downpour of rain, ‘Pour down mightily.’

13776.label: Job 37:7
13776.text: God puts a stop to all human activity So that every mortal man will know His work.

13777.label: Job 37:8
13777.text: The wild animals go into their densAnd remain in their lairs.

13778.label: Job 37:9
13778.text: The storm wind blows from its chamber, And the cold comes from the north winds.

13779.label: Job 37:10
13779.text: By the breath of God, the ice is produced, And the broad waters are frozen solid.

13780.label: Job 37:11
13780.text: Yes, he weighs down the clouds with moisture;He scatters his lightning in the clouds;

13781.label: Job 37:12
13781.text: They swirl around where he directs them;They carry out whatever he commands on the surface of the inhabited earth.

13782.label: Job 37:13
13782.text: Whether it is for punishment or for the sake of the landOr for loyal love, he causes it to happen.

13783.label: Job 37:14
13783.text: Listen to this, Job;Stop and consider carefully the wonderful works of God.

13784.label: Job 37:15
13784.text: Do you know how God controls the cloudsAnd how he causes the lightning to flash from his cloud?

13785.label: Job 37:16
13785.text: Do you know how the clouds float? These are the wonderful works of the One perfect in knowledge.

13786.label: Job 37:17
13786.text: Why does your clothing become hotWhen the earth is still because of the south wind?

13787.label: Job 37:18
13787.text: Can you, with him, spread out the skies As solid as a metal mirror?

13788.label: Job 37:19
13788.text: Tell us what we should say to him;We cannot answer because we are in the dark.

13789.label: Job 37:20
13789.text: Should he be told that I want to speak? Or has anyone said something that should be communicated to him?

13790.label: Job 37:21
13790.text: They cannot even see the light, Though it is bright in the sky,Until a wind passes by and clears away the clouds.

13791.label: Job 37:22
13791.text: Out of the north comes golden splendor;God’s majesty is awe-inspiring.

13792.label: Job 37:23
13792.text: Understanding the Almighty is beyond our reach; He is great in power, And he never violates his justice and abundant righteousness.

13793.label: Job 37:24
13793.text: Therefore, people should fear him. For he does not favor any who think that they are wise.”

13794.label: Job 38:1
13794.text: Then Jehovah answered Job out of the windstorm:

13795.label: Job 38:2
13795.text: “Who is this who is obscuring my counselAnd speaking without knowledge?

13796.label: Job 38:3
13796.text: Brace yourself, please, like a man;I will question you, and you inform me.

13797.label: Job 38:4
13797.text: Where were you when I founded the earth? Tell me, if you think you understand.

13798.label: Job 38:5
13798.text: Who set its measurements, in case you know,Or who stretched a measuring line across it?

13799.label: Job 38:6
13799.text: Into what were its pedestals sunk,Or who laid its cornerstone,

13800.label: Job 38:7
13800.text: When the morning stars joyfully cried out together,And all the sons of God began shouting in applause?

13801.label: Job 38:8
13801.text: And who barricaded the sea behind doors When it burst out from the womb,

13802.label: Job 38:9
13802.text: When I clothed it with cloudsAnd wrapped it in thick gloom,

13803.label: Job 38:10
13803.text: When I established my limit for itAnd put its bars and doors in place,

13804.label: Job 38:11
13804.text: And I said, ‘You may come this far, and no farther;Here is where your proud waves will stop’?

13805.label: Job 38:12
13805.text: Have you ever commanded the morningOr made the dawn know its place,

13806.label: Job 38:13
13806.text: To take hold of the ends of the earthAnd to shake the wicked out of it?

13807.label: Job 38:14
13807.text: It is transformed like clay under a seal,And its features stand out like those of a garment.

13808.label: Job 38:15
13808.text: But the light of the wicked is held back from them,And their uplifted arm is broken.

13809.label: Job 38:16
13809.text: Have you gone down to the sources of the seaOr explored the deep waters?

13810.label: Job 38:17
13810.text: Have the gates of death been revealed to you,Or have you seen the gates of deep darkness?

13811.label: Job 38:18
13811.text: Have you understood the vast expanse of the earth? Tell me, if you know all of this.

13812.label: Job 38:19
13812.text: In which direction does the light reside? And where is the place of darkness,

13813.label: Job 38:20
13813.text: That you should take it to its territoryAnd understand the paths to its home?

13814.label: Job 38:21
13814.text: Do you know this because you were already bornAnd the number of your years is great?

13815.label: Job 38:22
13815.text: Have you entered the storehouses of the snow, Or have you seen the storehouses of the hail,

13816.label: Job 38:23
13816.text: Which I have reserved for the time of distress,For the day of battle and war?

13817.label: Job 38:24
13817.text: From what direction is light dispersed,And from where does the east wind blow on the earth?

13818.label: Job 38:25
13818.text: Who has cut a channel for the floodAnd made a path for the thunderous storm cloud,

13819.label: Job 38:26
13819.text: To make it rain where no man lives,On the wilderness where there are no humans,

13820.label: Job 38:27
13820.text: To satisfy devastated wastelandsAnd cause the grass to sprout?

13821.label: Job 38:28
13821.text: Does the rain have a father, Or who fathered the dewdrops?

13822.label: Job 38:29
13822.text: From whose womb did the ice emerge,And who gave birth to the frost of heaven

13823.label: Job 38:30
13823.text: When the waters are covered as if with stone,And the surface of the deep waters is frozen solid?

13824.label: Job 38:31
13824.text: Can you tie the ropes of the Kiʹmah constellation Or untie the cords of the Keʹsil constellation?

13825.label: Job 38:32
13825.text: Can you lead out a constellation in its seasonOr guide the Ash constellation along with its sons?

13826.label: Job 38:33
13826.text: Do you know the laws governing the heavens, Or can you impose their authority on the earth?

13827.label: Job 38:34
13827.text: Can you raise your voice to the cloudsTo cause a flood of water to cover you?

13828.label: Job 38:35
13828.text: Can you send out lightning bolts? Will they come and say to you, ‘Here we are!’

13829.label: Job 38:36
13829.text: Who put wisdom within the clouds Or gave understanding to the sky phenomenon?

13830.label: Job 38:37
13830.text: Who is wise enough to count the clouds,Or who can tip over the water jars of heaven

13831.label: Job 38:38
13831.text: When the dust pours into a massAnd the clods of earth stick together?

13832.label: Job 38:39
13832.text: Can you hunt prey for a lionOr satisfy the appetites of young lions

13833.label: Job 38:40
13833.text: When they crouch in their lairsOr lie in ambush in their dens?

13834.label: Job 38:41
13834.text: Who prepares food for the raven When its young cry to God for helpAnd wander about because there is nothing to eat?

13835.label: Job 39:1
13835.text: “Do you know the time when the mountain goats give birth? Have you watched the deer give birth to their young?

13836.label: Job 39:2
13836.text: Do you count the months that they must complete? Do you know the time when they give birth?

13837.label: Job 39:3
13837.text: They crouch down when they give birth to their young,And their labor pains end.

13838.label: Job 39:4
13838.text: Their young become strong and grow up in the open field;They go out and do not return to them.

13839.label: Job 39:5
13839.text: Who set the wild donkey free, And who untied the ropes of the wild donkey?

13840.label: Job 39:6
13840.text: I have made the desert plain its homeAnd the salt land its dwelling.

13841.label: Job 39:7
13841.text: It scorns the tumult of the city;It does not hear the shouts of the driver.

13842.label: Job 39:8
13842.text: It roams the hills, seeking pasture,Looking for every green plant.

13843.label: Job 39:9
13843.text: Is the wild bull willing to serve you? Will it spend the night in your stable?

13844.label: Job 39:10
13844.text: Will you hold a wild bull to the furrow with a rope,Or will it follow you to plow the valley?

13845.label: Job 39:11
13845.text: Will you trust in its great strengthAnd let it do your heavy work?

13846.label: Job 39:12
13846.text: Will you rely on it to bring back your harvest, And will it gather it to your threshing floor?

13847.label: Job 39:13
13847.text: The wings of the ostrich flap joyfully,But can her pinions and plumage compare with the stork’s?

13848.label: Job 39:14
13848.text: For she leaves her eggs on the ground,And she keeps them warm in the dust.

13849.label: Job 39:15
13849.text: She forgets that some foot may crush themOr that a wild animal may trample them.

13850.label: Job 39:16
13850.text: She treats her sons harshly, as if they were not hers; She has no fear that her labor may be in vain.

13851.label: Job 39:17
13851.text: For God has deprived her of wisdomAnd given her no share in understanding.

13852.label: Job 39:18
13852.text: But when she rises up and flaps her wings,She laughs at the horse and at its rider.

13853.label: Job 39:19
13853.text: Are you the one who gives the horse its strength? Do you clothe its neck with a rustling mane?

13854.label: Job 39:20
13854.text: Can you cause it to leap like a locust? Its majestic snorting is terrifying.

13855.label: Job 39:21
13855.text: It paws the ground in the valley and exults mightily; It charges into the battle.

13856.label: Job 39:22
13856.text: It laughs at fear and is afraid of nothing. It does not turn back because of the sword.

13857.label: Job 39:23
13857.text: The quiver rattles against it,The spear and the javelin flash.

13858.label: Job 39:24
13858.text: Trembling with excitement, it surges forward, It cannot stand still at the sound of the horn.

13859.label: Job 39:25
13859.text: When the horn blows, it says, ‘Aha!’ It smells the battle from afarAnd hears the shouting of commanders and the battle cry.

13860.label: Job 39:26
13860.text: Is it by your understanding that the falcon soars,Spreading its wings to the south?

13861.label: Job 39:27
13861.text: Or is it at your order that an eagle flies upward And builds its nest high up,

13862.label: Job 39:28
13862.text: Spending the night on a cliff,Dwelling in its stronghold on a rocky crag?

13863.label: Job 39:29
13863.text: From there it searches for food; Its eyes look far into the distance.

13864.label: Job 39:30
13864.text: Its young sip up blood;And wherever the slain are, there it is.”

13866.label: Job 40:2
13866.text: “Should a faultfinder contend with the Almighty? Let the one who wants to reprove God answer.”

13867.label: Job 40:3
13867.text: Job said in answer to Jehovah:

13868.label: Job 40:4
13868.text: “Look! I am unworthy. What can I reply to you? I put my hand over my mouth.

13869.label: Job 40:5
13869.text: I spoke once, but I will not answer again;Twice, but I will say no more.”

13870.label: Job 40:6
13870.text: Then Jehovah answered Job out of the windstorm:

13871.label: Job 40:7
13871.text: “Brace yourself, please, like a man;I will question you, and you inform me.

13872.label: Job 40:8
13872.text: Will you call into question my justice? Will you condemn me so that you may be right?

13873.label: Job 40:9
13873.text: Do you have an arm as powerful as the true God’s, Or can your voice thunder like his?

13874.label: Job 40:10
13874.text: Adorn yourself, please, with glory and majesty;Clothe yourself with dignity and splendor.

13875.label: Job 40:11
13875.text: Release the fury of your anger;Look at everyone who is haughty, and bring him low.

13876.label: Job 40:12
13876.text: Look at everyone who is haughty, and humble him,And tread down the wicked where they stand.

13877.label: Job 40:13
13877.text: Hide them all in the dust;Bind them in the hidden place,

13878.label: Job 40:14
13878.text: Then even I would acknowledge to you That your right hand can save you.

13879.label: Job 40:15
13879.text: Here, now, is Be·heʹmoth, which I made as I made you. It eats grass like a bull.

13880.label: Job 40:16
13880.text: Look at the strength in its hipsAnd the power in the muscles of its belly!

13881.label: Job 40:17
13881.text: It stiffens its tail like a cedar;The sinews of its thighs are woven together.

13882.label: Job 40:18
13882.text: Its bones are tubes of copper;Its limbs are like wrought-iron rods.

13883.label: Job 40:19
13883.text: It ranks first among the works of God;Only its Maker can approach it with his sword.

13884.label: Job 40:20
13884.text: For the mountains produce food for it,Where all the wild animals play.

13885.label: Job 40:21
13885.text: It lies down under the lotus trees,In the shelter of the reeds of the marsh.

13886.label: Job 40:22
13886.text: The lotus trees cast their shadow on it,And the poplars of the valley surround it.

13887.label: Job 40:23
13887.text: If the river is turbulent, it does not panic. It is confident, although the Jordan rushes against its mouth.

13888.label: Job 40:24
13888.text: Can anyone capture it while it is watching,Or pierce its nose with a hook?

13889.label: Job 41:1
13889.text: “Can you catch Le·viʹa·than with a fishhookOr hold down its tongue with a rope?

13890.label: Job 41:2
13890.text: Can you put a rope through its nostrilsOr pierce its jaws with a hook?

13891.label: Job 41:3
13891.text: Will it make many pleas to you,Or will it speak gently to you?

13892.label: Job 41:4
13892.text: Will it make a covenant with you,So that you may make it your slave for life?

13893.label: Job 41:5
13893.text: Will you play with it as with a birdOr tie it on a leash for your little girls?

13894.label: Job 41:6
13894.text: Will traders barter for it? Will they divide it up among merchants?

13895.label: Job 41:7
13895.text: Will you fill its hide with harpoons Or its head with fishing spears?

13896.label: Job 41:8
13896.text: Lay your hand on it;You will remember the battle and never do it again!

13897.label: Job 41:9
13897.text: Any hope of subduing it is futile. The mere sight of it would overwhelm you.

13898.label: Job 41:10
13898.text: No one dares to stir it up. So who is it who can stand up to me?

13899.label: Job 41:11
13899.text: Who has given me anything first that I should repay him? Whatever is under the heavens is mine.

13900.label: Job 41:12
13900.text: I will not be silent about its limbs,About its mightiness and its well-formed body.

13901.label: Job 41:13
13901.text: Who has removed its outer covering? Who will enter its open jaws?

13902.label: Job 41:14
13902.text: Who can pry open the doors of its mouth? Its teeth all around are fearsome.

13903.label: Job 41:15
13903.text: Its back has rows of scales Tightly sealed together.

13904.label: Job 41:16
13904.text: Each one fits so closely to the otherThat no air can come between them.

13905.label: Job 41:17
13905.text: They are stuck to one another;They cling together and cannot be separated.

13906.label: Job 41:18
13906.text: Its snorting flashes out light,And its eyes are like the rays of dawn.

13907.label: Job 41:19
13907.text: Flashes of lightning go out of its mouth;Fiery sparks escape.

13908.label: Job 41:20
13908.text: Smoke pours out of its nostrils,Like a furnace fueled with rushes.

13909.label: Job 41:21
13909.text: Its breath sets coals ablaze,And a flame shoots from its mouth.

13910.label: Job 41:22
13910.text: There is great strength in its neck,And dismay runs before it.

13911.label: Job 41:23
13911.text: The folds of its flesh are tightly joined together;They are firm, as though cast upon it and immovable.

13912.label: Job 41:24
13912.text: Its heart is hard as stone,Yes, hard as a lower millstone.

13913.label: Job 41:25
13913.text: When it rises up, even the mighty are frightened;Its thrashing causes bewilderment.

13914.label: Job 41:26
13914.text: No sword that reaches it will prevail;Nor will spear, dart, or arrowhead.

13915.label: Job 41:27
13915.text: It regards iron as straw,Copper as rotten wood.

13916.label: Job 41:28
13916.text: An arrow does not make it flee;Slingstones turn into stubble against it.

13917.label: Job 41:29
13917.text: It regards a club as stubble,And it laughs at the rattling of a javelin.

13918.label: Job 41:30
13918.text: Underneath, it is like sharp fragments of pottery;It spreads itself in the mud like a threshing sledge.

13919.label: Job 41:31
13919.text: It makes the deep boil just like a pot;It stirs up the sea like an ointment pot.

13920.label: Job 41:32
13920.text: It leaves a glistening wake in its path. One would think that the deep had white hair.

13921.label: Job 41:33
13921.text: There is nothing like it on the earth,A creature made to have no fear.

13922.label: Job 41:34
13922.text: It glares at everything that is haughty. It is king over all the majestic wild beasts.”

13923.label: Job 42:1
13923.text: Then Job said in reply to Jehovah:

13924.label: Job 42:2
13924.text: “Now I know that you are able to do all thingsAnd that nothing you have in mind to do is impossible for you.

13925.label: Job 42:3
13925.text: You said, ‘Who is this who is obscuring my counsel without knowledge?’ Therefore I spoke, but without understandingAbout things too wonderful for me, which I do not know.

13926.label: Job 42:4
13926.text: You said, ‘Please listen, and I will speak. I will question you, and you inform me.’

13927.label: Job 42:5
13927.text: My ears have heard about you,But now I do see you with my eyes.

13928.label: Job 42:6
13928.text: That is why I take back what I said, And I repent in dust and ashes.”

13929.label: Job 42:7
13929.text: After Jehovah had spoken these words to Job, Jehovah said to Elʹi·phaz the Teʹman·ite: “My anger burns against you and your two companions, for you have not spoken the truth about me as my servant Job has.

13930.label: Job 42:8
13930.text: Now take seven bulls and seven rams and go to my servant Job, and offer up a burnt sacrifice for yourselves. And my servant Job will pray for you. I will surely accept his request not to deal with you according to your foolishness, for you have not spoken the truth about me as my servant Job has.”

13931.label: Job 42:9
13931.text: So Elʹi·phaz the Teʹman·ite, Bilʹdad the Shuʹhite, and Zoʹphar the Naʹa·ma·thite went and did what Jehovah had told them to do. And Jehovah accepted Job’s prayer.

13932.label: Job 42:10
13932.text: After Job had prayed for his companions, Jehovah removed Job’s tribulation and restored his prosperity. Jehovah gave him double what he had before.

13933.label: Job 42:11
13933.text: All his brothers and sisters and all his former friends came to him and ate a meal with him in his house. They sympathized with him and comforted him over all the calamity that Jehovah had allowed to come upon him. Each of them gave him a piece of money and a gold ring.

13934.label: Job 42:12
13934.text: So Jehovah blessed the last part of Job’s life more than the beginning, and Job came to have 14,000 sheep, 6,000 camels, 1,000 pairs of cattle, and 1,000 female donkeys.

13935.label: Job 42:13
13935.text: He also came to have seven more sons and three more daughters.

13936.label: Job 42:14
13936.text: He named the first daughter Je·miʹmah, the second Ke·ziʹah, and the third Kerʹen-hapʹpuch.

13937.label: Job 42:15
13937.text: No women in all the land were as beautiful as Job’s daughters, and their father gave them an inheritance along with their brothers.

13938.label: Job 42:16
13938.text: After this Job lived for 140 years, and he saw his children and his grandchildren—four generations.

13939.label: Job 42:17
13939.text: Finally Job died, after a long and satisfying life.
